why.treeMatures.fruits: Once grown, it fruits in its seasons, batch after batch.
why.payback.title: Has it paid for itself?
why.payback.lesson: A tree costs now and pays for years: that's an investment.
why.sapling.title: {tree} sapling
why.sapling.planting: The price includes digging and planting it.
why.cash.title: Cash
why.cash.quiet: No money in or out yet today.
why.cash.lesson: Cash is not profit: paying ahead or buying stock moves cash without being a cost yet.
why.store.title: Your store
why.store.room: The hut holds a fixed weight. What doesn't fit waits where it is or sells to the trader.
why.store.lesson: Sell before the store fills, or a harvest has nowhere to go.
why.price.index: Prices this year (they rise a little each season)
why.traderPrice.title: What the trader pays for {good}
why.traderPrice.lesson: The trader buys at the valley's price less the carting, up to what he can take each day.
why.orderPrice.title: What the supermarket pays for {good}
why.orderPrice.lesson: A buyer who pays more wants something back: produce harvested today, the amount it asks for, by midnight.
why.owed.title: The supermarket owes you
why.owed.when: Booked as a sale when you delivered; the cash comes at 6:00.
why.owed.lesson: A sale isn't cash until it's paid. Money owed to you still counts in what you're worth.
why.truck.title: The trader's truck
why.truck.price: His price is set at 6:00 and holds all day.
why.truckRoom.title: What the trader still takes of {good}
why.truckRoom.day: He buys this much of it a day
why.truckRoom.text: He takes the smaller of the two: what is left of the day's room for this crop, or what is left on the truck.
why.truck.lesson: Sell in the morning and you know the price. Big harvests are what the store and the mandi are for.
why.marketPrice.title: {good} on the village market
why.marketPrice.floor: It never stays far below what the trader pays
why.marketPrice.ceiling: Or far above what bringing it in costs
why.marketPrice.offered: What's on offer, yours included, pushes the price down.
why.marketPrice.town: Your town buys about this much a day
why.marketPrice.demand: With nothing on offer, the price sits at the valley's.
why.marketPrice.lesson: Offer a little at a time: a glut sinks the price to the trader's.
why.traderRoom.title: The trader can still take
why.traderRoom.lesson: His room comes back each morning.
why.spoilage.title: Spoils by tomorrow
why.spoilage.offer: Stock you've offered at the market spoils last.
why.spoilage.lesson: Grain keeps; potatoes, fruit and greens don't. Sell the quick spoilers first.
why.input.title: {good} in store
why.input.use: It counts as a cost when you sow or spray with it.
why.input.lesson: Buying ahead swaps cash for stock: your profit isn't touched until you use it.
why.inputPrice.title: {good} costs
why.inputPrice.lesson: Seed is dearer at sowing time: buying ahead saves money.
why.mandi.title: The mandi trip
why.mandi.0: At the town mandi your goods fetch the valley's price when the trolley gets back, {hours} hours after it leaves.
why.mandi.1: The commission agent keeps {pct} of the sale.
why.mandi.2: A tractor-trolley is hired for the trip; it carries up to {kg}.
why.mandi.3: Going takes half an hour of your day, once a day at most.
why.mandi.4: The village trader pays less, but at once and with no trip.
why.mandi.5: Your cart is at the mandi. It is sold at the valley's price when it gets back, less the commission agent's {pct}; the trolley's hire was paid when it left. The figure is an estimate at today's price: the sale uses the price at that moment.
why.mandi.lesson: A trip pays when the load is big enough to cover the trolley.
why.netWorth.title: What you own minus what you owe
why.netWorth.book: In your books (land and goods at what they cost)
why.netWorth.lesson: Net worth grows when what you earn beats what you spend and owe.
why.credit.title: {lender}: you can borrow
why.credit.base: Lends anyone in the village up to
why.credit.land: Land you bought counts for ({pct} of its value)
why.credit.inherited: Your family's land can never be pledged.
why.credit.tooLow: Your score is below what this lender accepts.
why.credit.lesson: Borrow only for what earns more than the interest.
why.loan.title: {lender}: still owed
why.loan.bullet: Interest each season; the whole loan back with the last payment.
why.loan.instalments: A part of the loan back each season, with its interest.
why.loan.lesson: A missed payment costs late interest and your score.
why.borrow.title: Paying back over
why.borrow.lesson: A longer term means smaller payments but more interest in all.
why.calendar.title: The calendar
why.calendar.words: A season lasts {season} days and a year {year}.
why.calendar.clock: The game's clock matches your phone's: the farm keeps working while the app is closed.
why.calendar.away: Away longer than {hours} hours, the farm waits for you.
why.calendar.lesson: One hour here is about a day in the valley.
why.forecast.title: How sure is this?
why.forecast.runs: Weather comes in runs: calm weather lasts, storms pass in an hour or two.
why.forecast.lesson: Plan on today's forecast; keep a margin for the days after.
why.saved.title: Saving
why.saved.when: The game saves every hour, a few seconds after your last tap, and when you leave the app.
why.saved.backups: It keeps backups, so a crash never costs more than an hour.
why.labour.title: Your work today
why.labour.lesson: Eat well and rest: a tired, hungry founder gets less done.
why.health.title: Health
why.health.cold: No warm clothes in Winter takes
why.health.sick: The lower your health, the likelier a sick day.
why.health.lesson: Medicine helps once a day; good food helps every day.
why.fatigue.title: Tiredness
why.fatigue.lesson: Long days add up; a rest day takes tiredness away.
why.diet.title: {plan} food plan
why.diet.food: Home-grown food can pay this much of it
why.diet.paid: Paid at the start of the season.
why.diet.lesson: Cheap food costs work: you get less done each day.
why.hours.title: {option}
why.dayLabour.title: Day labour pays about
why.dayLabour.fields: Those hours come off your own fields.
why.dayLabour.lesson: Day labour is sure money; your own fields may earn more.
why.medicine.title: Medicine
why.medicine.once: One dose a day helps; more doesn't.
why.hire.title: Labourers till harvest
why.hire.until: Until the last crop growing now is ready, in
why.hire.care: Their hours join yours in caring for the fields.
why.hire.leave: They harvest each field without an order as it ripens, then go home.
why.hire.fodder: A fodder field doesn't count: it isn't harvested but cut each morning with the animals' work.
why.handSkill.title: Skill
why.handSkill.grows: Skill grows with every season worked.
why.handSkill.lesson: A hand who stays gets better.
why.handHours.title: A hand's work
why.handHours.skill: A more skilled hand gets more done in a day; so does a keen, rested one (their Output says why). Long days add 2 hours.
why.handHours.acre: About 3 hours a day tends an acre of wheat.
why.handWage.title: Wage a season
why.handWage.paid: Paid at the start of each season, for the season ahead.
why.handWage.inKindNext: The family's house becomes part of the pay at the next renewal: {house} less in cash.
why.handWage.lesson: A hand pays when the acres they tend earn more than the wage.
why.handLapse.title: Unpaid wage
why.handLapse.what: The contract lapsed: the hand waits a while for the wage before leaving.
why.handLapse.backPay: Renewing now pays what is owed.
why.handPrepaid.title: Wage paid ahead
why.handPrepaid.what: The part of this season's wage not yet worked.
why.handPrepaid.lesson: Paying ahead is cash out now; the cost counts day by day.
why.hut.title: A hand's hut
why.hut.what: A hand needs a hut in the labour quarters.
why.applicant.title: What you know of them
why.applicant.range: Until you talk, you only know their skill roughly.
why.orderMin.title: Lowest price
why.orderMin.what: Your hand won't sell below this at the market.
why.orderMin.floor: Below the trader's price, the trader buys anyway.
why.free.title: Labourers free today
why.free.pool: Neighbouring villages send a few each day.
why.away.title: While you were away
why.away.Ready: Crops, beds and trees that ripened while you were away wait for you to collect them.
why.away.Sales: Your offers at the market sold hour by hour; the trader bought at his price.
why.away.DayLabour: You worked on neighbours' farms as planned.
why.away.HomeUse: Your family ate from the store: food you didn't have to buy.
why.away.Spoiled: Goods lose a little each day in the store; a ready crop starts to spoil after three days.
why.away.Pests: Pests found a crop. Spray it to limit the damage.
why.away.Sick: On a sick day you rest.
why.away.Seasons: A season closed: its report shows how the farm did.
why.away.Index: Prices rise a little each season.
why.away.People: Your hands worked through their orders.
why.away.Truck: The trader's truck came at 6:00 and bought at the day's price till midnight or till it was full.
why.away.Orders: The supermarket's orders: what you or your hands delivered was paid at 6:00 the next morning. What wasn't delivered by midnight ran out, with no penalty.
why.away.Held: Your hands kept what they harvested while the truck was away, and sold it to the truck when it came at 6:00.
why.away.lesson: The farm keeps going while you're away, for up to three days.
why.report.farmCosts: Inputs count when used, not when bought.
why.report.household: Living costs come before anything else.
why.report.finance: A loan helps only if what it buys earns more than this.
why.report.other: Losses on things sold or gone.
why.report.netResult: This is your profit for the season.
account.CropSales: Crops sold and eaten at home
account.FruitSales: Fruit sold and eaten at home
account.Depreciation: Wear and tear on buildings and machines
why.gardenSeason.title: Picked from this bed this season
why.gardenSeason.total: A bed gives in a season
why.gardenSeason.rest: Once it has given its season's worth, the bed rests until the next season.
why.order.title: {name}'s order
why.order.what: An order is a job your hand does by themselves: sow, harvest, pick and sell.
why.order.hour: A hand does one thing an hour on each order.
why.order.never: A hand never undoes a crop you sowed yourself.
why.post.title: Sending word for a hand
why.post.what: Word goes round the neighbouring villages: for a few days people come asking for work more often.
why.post.above: Offering above the usual wage brings better, surer people, who ask for more.

equipment.upkeepOff: Skipped: it breaks down more often
equipment.sellNote: At 80% of its book value; the bank is repaid first if it backs a loan

machineLoan.why: The bank lends against the machine itself, at 70% of its value
machineLoan.diesel: And this season's diesel, paid now
why.machine.title: A new {machine}
why.machine.acres: Fields it works (the well acres first)
why.machine.labour: Work saved on a field it works
why.machine.tools: Harvest of a crop sown with it (on time)
why.machine.cart: Takes to the mandi without the hired trolley
why.machine.bullocks: Bullocks that pull it (in the second shed)
why.machine.diesel: Diesel a season, each field it works
why.machine.upkeep: Maintenance a season, of its price
why.machine.breaks: Chance it breaks down a day (maintained · maintenance skipped)
why.machine.repair: A repair costs, of its price
why.machine.lesson: Buying costs most upfront and loses value each season; leasing and hiring cost more over time but never break on you. On a small farm, hiring on sowing days is often cheaper.
why.machineValue.title: What it's worth
why.machineValue.market: What a buyer pays ({share} of book)
why.machineValue.lesson: Depreciation spreads a machine's cost over the seasons it works: a cost in your season report, though no cash leaves.
why.fieldTools.title: Who works this field
why.fieldTools.hand: Your family and hands with hand tools. A machine from the Menu → Equipment cuts the work and helps sow on time.
why.fieldTools.hired: Hired for today: it works all your fields until midnight.
why.fieldTools.tools: Harvest of a crop sown now
why.fieldTools.lesson: A crop keeps the harvest boost of the machine it was sown with.

menu.businesses.note: Start a business, see how yours are doing
lands.title: Your land
lands.subtitle: Parcels for sale in the valley
lands.none: There's no land for sale right now.
lands.hillsNote: Apples grow here · no lane yet
lands.notNext: Not next to your land yet
money.title: Money and loans
money.loanValue: Owes {owed} · {next} due at the season's end
season.head: {head} · {amount}
season.farmProfit: Of that, the farm's own profit
season.profit.why: This is the season report's last line, What's left after everything: it counts your family's living and interest too. The farm's own profit is the one the Hamlet asks for.
season.profit.lesson: Profit and cash are different things: Why your cash moved differently shows the gap.
season.cashValueLast: {start} at the start → {end} at the end
season.cash.lesson: Cash at the start + profit + each line above = your cash.
season.nothingDue: Nothing is due at the season's end
season.short: Short by {amount}: {who}. Sell from the store, or borrow on Your wealth
season.short.living: your family would drop to the subsistence plan
season.due.why: Everything the season's close takes from your cash, in the order it takes it, at the prices the close will charge (prices rise a little each season, and that is counted here). Seed and feed are bought as you go, so they aren't counted. A business pays its own charges from its own cash.
season.due.lesson: Rent from your families comes in after these are paid, so don't count on it here.
season.due.owed: Coming from the supermarket at 6:00, not counted here
season.due.loan.why: What the loan asks at the season's end.
season.due.principal: Principal: paying back what you borrowed, not a cost
season.due.living.why: Next season's food and basics on your plan, paid at the season's end.
season.due.renewal.why: Next season's wage, paid upfront at the season's end. Without the cash, the contract lapses.
season.due.house: The house, part of the pay
season.own: Your businesses pay these from their own cash
season.own.why: Not counted in what's due from you: a business pays its own worker, loan and pitch from its own cash and overdraft. Put cash in if it is short.
season.own.canSpend: Its cash and overdraft room now
season.own.short: Short by {amount}: put cash in before the season's end
season.due.warehouse.why: Rent for the grain space your goods need past your own godown, paid upfront at the season's end. Without it the space ends and the goods go back to the hut store.
season.due.water.why: What your water costs to run next season, paid at the season's end. Unpaid, that source stays off for the season.
season.due.school.why: A gift to the village, paid at the season's end. Unpaid, the district carries the school this season.
season.due.machine.lease.why: The {machine}'s lease and its diesel for next season, paid at the season's end. Unpaid, it goes back to its owner.
season.due.machine.upkeep.why: Servicing keeps the {machine}'s breakdown chance low. Skipped, it breaks down more often.
season.due.machine.diesel.why: Diesel for the {machine}'s acres next season. Unpaid, it stands idle.
season.short.warehouse: your goods would go back to the hut store
season.short.water.canal: the canal's channels would stay dry
season.short.school: the district would carry the school
season.short.machine.lease: the {machine} would go back to its owner
season.orders.why: What the supermarket's orders paid, good by good. It pays at 6:00 the next morning.
season.good.why: Where it sold, at the day's price.
season.good.mandi: The mandi's figure is before its commission, which is under Spent.
season.soldTo.Lender: Taken and sold by the lender
season.homeUse: Your family ate from the store
season.otherSales.why: Sales from before this record began.
season.MilkSales.why: Milk to the co-op, to your dairy and drunk at home.
season.LivestockSales.why: Calves sold at the cattle fair.
season.DayLabourEarnings.why: What neighbours paid you for days on their farms.
season.RentReceived.why: Families pay rent for your houses at the season's end.
season.BusinessDrawingsIncome.why: What you took out of your businesses beyond what you put in.
season.GainOnAssetSales.why: Sold for more than its value in your books.
season.DebtWrittenOff.why: What lenders let go after a foreclosure.
season.SeedsAndPlanting.why: Seed and saplings as you sow and plant them. Seed in the store isn't a cost until it's sown.
season.FertiliserAndSpraying.why: Fertiliser, compost and spray as they're used.
season.AnimalFeed.why: Feed and straw your animals ate.
season.LivingCosts.why: Food and basics, paid at the season's start and counted day by day.
season.Rent.why: Rent for land or a pitch you use.
season.Interest.why: What borrowing cost this season, counted day by day.
season.Depreciation.why: A building's cost spread over its life, counted at the season's end. No cash leaves.
season.LossOnAssetSales.why: Sold for less than its value in your books, or trees removed.
season.TransportAndSelling.why: The mandi's commission and the cart.
season.Power.why: Power for the pump, the borewell and drip, the canal's water fee, and the diesel for your tractor on neighbours' acres.
season.Repairs.why: Upkeep of your drip lines, and repairs.
season.wage.why: Paid upfront at the season's start and counted day by day: what's still to come is under Paid ahead.
season.labourers.why: Labourers hired for the harvest, from your town and nearby villages.
season.moved.paidAhead: Paid ahead, still to be used
season.moved.paidAhead.why: Wages and living paid at the season's start for the days still to come, and inputs bought into the store. The cash has gone, but each counts as a cost only when it's used.
season.moved.wear.why: Wear is a cost under Spent, but no cash left your hands.
season.moved.owed.why: Delivered and counted as earned; the supermarket pays at 6:00.
season.moved.interestOwed: Interest owed, paid at the season's end
season.moved.interestOwed.why: Interest counts as it runs; the lender is paid at the season's end.
season.moved.interestPaid.why: Interest counted in an earlier season, paid this one.
season.moved.repaid: Paid back on loans: not a cost
season.moved.repaid.why: Paying back what you borrowed, not a cost: you owe that much less.
season.moved.borrowed.why: A loan isn't income: you'll pay it back.
season.moved.boughtBuildings.why: You still own it: it's in Your wealth, not a cost. Its wear counts a little each season.
season.moved.herdGrowth.why: Your heifers grew in worth. It is in what you earned above, but no money came in: you get it only if you sell them.
season.moved.boughtLivestock.why: You still own them: they're in Your wealth, not a cost.
season.moved.boughtTrees.why: You still own them: they're in Your wealth, not a cost.
season.moved.boughtLand.why: You still own it: it's in Your wealth, not a cost.
season.moved.boughtEquipment.why: You still own them: they're in Your wealth, not a cost.
season.moved.boughtInvestmentInBusinesse: Put into your businesses: still yours
You still own it: it's in Your wealth, not a cost.
season.moved.sold: Sold: cash for what you owned
season.moved.sold.why: What you owned, at its value in your books; any gain or loss is under Earned or Spent.
season.moved.fromBusiness.why: Cash you put in, taken back out: not income.
season.moved.other.why: Anything else that moved your cash.

why.irrigation.unpaid: Its power went unpaid at the season's end, so it's off until the next one.
why.irrigation.drip: Drip holds the crop at the lowest moisture it grows well in, and never floods it.
why.irrigation.dripCare: Care saved each day (no weeding between the lines)

why.irrigation.buckets: Your buckets keep it at least at

why.irrigation.rainFed: Only the rain waters this acre.

why.godown.waits: What gains by waiting: rice and maize from the Monsoon harvest till Spring or Summer, mustard from Winter till Summer. Wheat ripens in Winter, when it's dearest, so sell it then.

letter.welcome: My dear beta, the farm is yours now. Six acres by the river, the hut your grandfather built, and the well that never failed us. The fields have rested too long and the soil is tired, but it is honest: it gives back what you put in. You'll find seed potato, some wheat and lentils, and greens seed in the store, and a little money to begin. Start small.
letter.garden: By the door is the baadi, our kitchen garden. Radish, spinach, coriander: they grow in minutes and feed the house. Sow one bed now; by the time you've looked around, it will be ready.
letter.household: A farm runs on the people who work it, and you are the first. Choose how the house eats and how long you work: good food and rest let you do more, day after day. The house eats from the store first. Your grandfather kept wheat and lentils from his last harvest; if you'd rather sow them than eat them, switch 'eat from the store' off for now.
letter.firstPick: There: your first basket. Everything you pick goes to the store, where it waits for you. Greens don't keep long, so eat them or sell them soon.
letter.firstSale: The trader comes to the gate every day and buys at a fair, low price. That's money today. His truck comes every morning at 6:00 and leaves at midnight. Later you'll learn when it pays to wait, or to take a cart to the mandi in town.
letter.longCrop: Now something that takes longer. Potato does well in Spring on the well acres, and the seed is already in the store. It takes about 15 hours. Crops wait in the field when they're ready, but not forever: after three days they start to spoil.
letter.comeBack: That's a good first day. The farm keeps going while you're away: the crops grow, the house eats, the trader buys. Your {crop} will be ready {time}.{quick} Want a nudge when it's ready? Never at night.
letter.comeBack.on: That's a good first day. The farm keeps going while you're away: the crops grow, the house eats, the trader buys. Your {crop} will be ready {time}.{quick}
letter.comeBack.quick: Your other acres needn't wait: sown now, {crops}.
letter.firstReturn: Welcome back. Here's what happened while you were away. Tap Collect all to bring in what's ready.
letter.firstFieldHarvest: Your first field harvest. Tap the ? beside it to see what made it: the soil, the water, your care, the weather, the seed. The weakest of them holds the rest back.
letter.pest: Pests on one of your fields. Spray now and you'll save most of the crop; leave it and you'll lose some. Fields that grow the same crop again and again draw more pests.
letter.sellOrStore: Your store is filling up. Three ways to sell: the trader at the gate (today, at his price), the village market (a little at a time, at a better price), or a cart to the mandi (a full load, half a day away, after the cart's hire). Or keep it for a better season, if it keeps.
letter.seasonReport: Your first season is done. The report shows whether the farm paid for itself. Money you paid ahead for next season isn't a cost yet, so cash and profit tell different stories.
letter.labour: Your fields need more hands than yours. A labourer from the next village stays for one crop, till its harvest; a farm hand stays for the season but needs a hut to live in. A Hamlet begins with a hand's house.
letter.borrowing: Money is short for what you want to do next. The moneylender lends quickly, at a high price. The bank lends more, cheaper, if you can show land or a good season. Borrow only what the work will pay back.
letter.sick: You're unwell today and the fields will wait. Eat well, rest, and the chemist in the village has medicine.
letter.hamlet: Look at what you've built: six acres in good heart, a house for a hand, a season that paid its way. This isn't a homestead any more. It's a Hamlet, and you can keep cattle now: tap your cattle yard beside the house. A Village needs more: five households on your land, a business that pays its way two seasons, and a school for the children. Your letter in the Menu keeps count.
letter.village: Beta, your grandfather used to say a village isn't its fields, it's its people. Look around: five families make their homes on your land, your {business} has paid its way, and the children walk to the school you gave them. It's a Village now. New trades open to you: a bakery, a dairy and a brick kiln, stalls on the square, drip and a borewell for the fields, a tractor, and the co-op bank will lend you more. Grow it with care: every family here counts on you.
letter.firstOrders: A shop in the city buys fresh produce straight from farms. It pays more than the trader, but only for what you harvest today, delivered by midnight, and it pays the next morning.
letter.truckAway: The trader's truck comes at 6:00 and leaves at midnight, or when it's full. The stall closes at night too. Keep it in the store, or take a cart to the mandi.

why.era.title: Becoming a Hamlet
why.era.acres: Field harvests on different acres you own count, all in the same season. A second harvest on the same acre doesn't add an acre. A new season starts the count again.
why.era.care: The average Care of every field harvest this season, as a share of what the crops needed. More hands than the crops need lift it a little; too few hold it back.
why.era.hut: A hand's hut in the labour quarters, finished. One being built doesn't count yet.
why.era.profit: Any closed season whose farm profit was above nothing: the farm earned more than its seed, inputs, wages and upkeep cost.
why.village.title: Becoming a Village
why.village.households: A household is a family in a house on your land, or a hand alone in his hut. Build a family house and a family moves in: the co-op bank lends on the house, and the rent pays the loan back.
why.village.business: A season counts when the business's own books show a profit after its costs and wages, in any two seasons. Start a flour mill; its Books show each season.
why.village.school: Build the school on the school plot, from cash or with a co-op loan.
why.village.lesson: Quickest: homes first, then a business, then the school. The bank lends on a house and its rent repays it; borrow for a business first and the bank has less left for houses.
why.era.lesson: Six acres is more than one founder can tend: the Hamlet starts when you hire.

why.heiferKeep.how: A heifer is kept only if a place in the shed is free; if the shed is full she is sold at the fair, and a bull calf always is. She takes her place and her feed until her first calving.
why.heiferKeep.lesson: Raising your own cows costs about what buying one does, and takes years. What you gain is cash spread over time, and a herd that grows without a purchase.

why.heiferRaise.lesson: Home-grown fodder is the cheap part of a cow's feed. Raise heifers when you grow your own and a place stands empty.

why.heiferGrowing.growing: She is fed enough, so each morning counts as a day grown.
why.heiferGrowing.waiting: She was not fed enough this morning, so tomorrow does not count as a day grown. Fill the feed room and she grows again; no day is lost for good, and her health only falls after two hungry days.
why.heiferGrowing.lesson: A heifer grows only on a day she is fed.
why.heiferWorth.title: What {name} is worth now
why.heiferWorth.how: Her worth rises a little each morning, to the day she calves. It is on your books as herd growth, but it is not cash: you get it only if you sell her, and then at the fair's share of it.
why.heiferWorth.lesson: A growing herd is an asset that gains worth before it earns. Books count it; your wallet does not.

story.why.title: A story from your valley
story.why.stall.1: A hand or worker of yours for {seasons} seasons or more, whose family has put aside {savings} or more and who is paid fairly, has a {chance} chance each season of giving notice. They will go at the next close, with no severance, and you hire again or run the post yourself.
story.why.stall.2: At the close they left, the story opened their stall itself, on a free pitch or by the lane, so nobody leaves for nothing. It is the village's stall, a rival of yours, and it follows the usual shop rules.
story.why.stall.3: {after} seasons after they left, the stall is looked at: still open is doing well, closed means they look for wages again.
story.why.reader.1: A child of your households has started school and nobody in the family can read yet.
story.why.reader.2: They learned to read, and were the first in the family to do so.
story.why.reader.3: At {age} or older they took a paid job or a hire with you.

story.why.migrant.2: The same family has stayed {second} seasons.

story.why.longlife.3: A life-year passes each season. This is a person reaching a round age still in your town.

story.why.rule: At most one story step happens a season in the whole town, in this order: a stall, a first reader, a migrant family, a long life. Nothing is random but whether a hand gives notice, and nothing here is asked of you.

almanac.why.worthNow: Everything you own less what you owe, at this Winter's close
almanac.why.worthRule: Net worth is the same figure as on your Winter season report: cash, land, buildings, stock and your businesses, less loans.
almanac.why.quiet: No business or crop earned {min} or more this year, so there is no best return. A small profit on a small sum is still a quiet year.
almanac.why.bestProfitBusiness: What the business earned over the year's four seasons
almanac.why.bestPutBusiness: The money you put into it, still in the business
almanac.why.bestProfitCrop: What its sales earned, less what you put in
almanac.why.bestPutCrop: Its seed and fertiliser this year, and its share of the year's hired labour (shared among your crops by how many fields each was sown on)
almanac.why.bestRule: The best return is the biggest share of profit to money put in, among your businesses and your crops, counted from {min} of profit. So a small business that did well can beat a big one that did not.
almanac.why.lossNone: No fire repair, no loss on a sale or a closing, no seizure, no day of spoiled goods and no losing season stood out this year.
almanac.why.lossRule: Only one-off losses count: a fire's repair, a loss on selling or closing a business or a machine, a day's spoiled goods, something seized for a debt, a business's losing season. Wages, seed, rent and fuel never do.
almanac.why.spot.1: Their own story moved a step this year: a hand saving for a stall, a first reader, a migrant family, a long life. The latest step comes first.
almanac.why.spot.2: The first child to learn to read at your school this year.
almanac.why.spot.3: The youngest baby born to your families this year.
almanac.why.spot.4: The one of your hands and workers who has been with you the longest.
almanac.why.spot.5: The oldest of your people living in the valley.
almanac.why.spotNone: No child learned to read, no baby was born, nobody works for you and nobody is old enough yet.
almanac.why.spotRule: One person a year, the first that fits in this order: a story that moved, the first child to read, the youngest baby, your longest-serving worker, your oldest elder. Equal cases go to whoever came first. Nothing is random.
almanac.why.foot: An Almanac is written once, at the Winter close, and never changes. The last 8 are kept.

why.townHappiness.title: Your town's happiness
why.townHappiness.mean: The average over everyone: a bigger family counts for more.
why.townHappiness.lesson: Happy people stay; each family's card shows what would help.
why.employment.title: Work in town
why.employment.what: Adults with a job here: your hands. The others work outside, on about half the days.
why.employment.outside: Outside work pays a day, on average
why.employment.lesson: A job in town is steadier than outside work, so it makes families happier.
why.householdIncome.title: Income this season
why.householdIncome.remit: Half sent home to the family
why.householdIncome.lesson: A family's income sets everything else: food first, then the rest.
why.householdBudget.title: The season's budget
why.householdBudget.engel: Engel's law: the less a family earns for each person, the bigger the share it spends on food.
why.householdBudget.lesson: As incomes rise, food takes a smaller share and more is left for everything else.
why.householdSavings.title: Savings
why.householdSavings.first: In a short season, savings buy the food first.
why.householdSavings.lesson: Savings carry a family through a bad season.
why.householdRent.title: Rent
why.householdRent.hut: A hand's hut is part of the pay: no rent.
why.householdRent.inKind: The house is part of the hand's pay: no rent.
why.householdRent.how: Paid at each season's close, from the budget first, then from savings.
why.householdRent.leave: A family {n} seasons behind may move away: half do, at each close. They owe nothing when they go.
why.householdRent.lesson: Rent pays back what the house cost, season by season.
why.householdHappiness.title: Happiness
why.householdHappiness.weights: Weights: food and a home {a}, a safe living {b}, belonging {c}, getting on {d}.
why.householdHappiness.gate: Each layer counts fully only once the one below it is met to {gate}.
why.householdHappiness.leave: A family below {below} at {n} closes in a row may move away: half do, at each close.
why.householdHappiness.lesson: People need food and a home before anything else.
why.citizenAge.title: Age
why.citizenAge.season: People age a year each season ({n} at each season's close).
why.citizenAge.stages: Children till {adult}, adults till {elder}, then elders.
why.citizenAge.lesson: A season is 4 days, so children grow up within weeks of play.
why.citizenHealth.title: Health
why.citizenHealth.food: Health falls in a season without enough food and comes back when they eat well.
why.citizenHealth.later: Doctors and a clinic come later.
why.citizenJob.title: Work
why.citizenJob.outside: Outside work pays a day, on average
why.citizenJob.hire: When you hire labourers, your town's own come first.
why.citizenJob.literate: They can read, so outside work pays them {pct} more.
why.businessArea.title: The area's grain a day
why.businessArea.people: People who'd bring their grain (your town {town})
why.businessArea.each: Grain a person brings a day
why.businessArea.hours: They come between 8:00 and 18:00, a little each hour.
why.businessArea.lost: Grain your mill can't grind that hour goes to the next village's chakki.
why.businessArea.lesson: A village chakki lives on the area's grinding, not on its owner's wheat.
why.businessFee.title: The next village's fee
why.businessFee.next: There's no chakki nearer: people carry their grain to the next village's, which charges this.
why.businessFee.most: Charge no more than this, or they keep going there
why.businessFee.lesson: Customers compare prices: a little dearer and they walk on.
why.businessTrader.title: {good} at the trader
why.businessTrader.day: He takes at most a day
why.businessWage.title: A {role}'s wage a season
why.businessWage.paid: Paid at the start of each season from the business's own cash.
why.businessWage.who: The best-skilled adult in your town without a job here takes it; if there's nobody, a worker comes daily from a neighbouring village.
why.businessWage.you: Run it yourself and there's no wage, but your hours there come off your farm.
why.businessOwn.title: Your wheat a day
why.businessOwn.price: The mill pays your farm today's trader price
why.businessOwn.books: It's a sale on your farm's books and stock on the mill's: each keeps its own books.
why.businessOwn.yields: A kilo of wheat gives 0.97 kg of atta and 0.03 kg of bran.
why.businessOwn.lesson: Turning your own harvest into something worth more is where processing pays.
why.businessWorker.title: Who works here
why.businessWorker.you: You run it: it's open only in your hours there, and those come off your farm work.
why.businessWorker.neighbour: Nobody in your town was free, so a worker comes daily from a neighbouring village.
why.businessWorker.town: One of your people works here: a job in town for their family.
why.businessWorker.townJob: A job at your business counts as a job in town.
why.businessHours.title: Open hours
why.businessHours.area: People bring their grain between 8:00 and 18:00: closed in those hours, theirs goes to the next village.
why.businessHours.worker: The worker works the hours you set. Hours past 8:00–18:00 are overtime, paid at time and a half as they're worked, and long days tire them.
why.businessHours.you: You're at the mill these hours, so they come off your farm work.
why.businessMarket.title: Wheat at the market
why.businessMarket.price: Wheat bought in costs the market's price with its transport: a little atta margin is left.
why.businessMarket.lesson: Milling bought wheat keeps the chakki busy but pays thinly.
why.businessMarket.cap: The trader takes only {atta} of atta and {bran} of bran a day, and the village does not buy from the mill. So the mill buys wheat at the market only while its unsold atta and bran stay under {days} days of that; more would only fill the yard with goods it cannot sell.
why.businessCash.title: The mill's cash
why.businessCash.own: The mill's own money, apart from yours: what you put in, fees and sales in, wheat, power and wages out.
why.businessCash.flow: Cash isn't profit: the machine was paid for at once but wears out over years.
why.businessCash.lesson: A business can make a profit and still run short of cash.
why.books.title: {line}, {period}
why.books.fees: The area's grain ground: {area}, at your fee of {fee} a kg. The grain stays theirs: you're paid for the work.
why.books.sales: What the trader's truck and your feed room paid for the atta and bran made from {own} of wheat.
why.books.goods: What the wheat in the atta and bran sold cost. Your own wheat comes in at the market price (a sale on your farm's books); what isn't sold yet stays in stock.
why.books.margin: Fees and sales less the cost of the wheat sold. It has to pay the running costs.
why.books.wages: The {role}'s wage, paid upfront for the season. Run by you, there's no wage: your hours there come off your farm work.
why.books.power: {kg} ground, at {power} a kg for the motor.
why.books.repairs: {share} of the equipment's value a season, paid at the close.
why.books.depreciation: The building ({building} over {buildingLife} seasons) and the equipment ({equipment} over {equipmentLife} seasons) wear out a little each season. No cash moves: it was paid when you built.
why.books.interest: Interest on the overdraft and the business loan.
why.books.profit: The gross margin less the running costs: wages, power, repairs, wear and interest.
why.books.cashStart: The cash it had when the season began.
why.books.cashIn: Fees, sales and any cash you put in.
why.books.cashOut: Wheat, power, wages, repairs and any cash you took out.
why.books.cashEnd: Cash at the start, plus money in, less money out.
why.books.stock: Wheat, atta and bran in stock, at what they cost.
why.books.fixed: What the building and equipment cost, less their wear so far.
why.books.debts: The overdraft and the business loan.
why.books.capital: The cash you've put in, less what you've taken out.
why.books.kept: The profits it has made and kept, less any losses.
why.books.worth: What it owns less what it owes. Your net worth counts it at this, never below 0.
why.books.pnlLesson: A business keeps its own books: its profit is its own, apart from your farm's.
why.books.cashLesson: Cash is not profit: the building was paid for once in cash but wears out a little each season, and stock is cash waiting to be sold.
why.books.balanceLesson: What a business owns = what it owes + what's yours in it.
why.booksPlan.wait: After {n} full seasons, each line's average a season is set against the plan you made on founding day, with why they differ.
why.booksPlan.title: {line}, a season
why.booksPlan.actual: Actual: the average of the last {n} seasons
why.booksPlan.lesson: A plan is a guess at today's prices: checking it against what happened is how you plan better next time.
why.plan.cost.title: Building and machine
why.plan.cost: A small shed and a 10 HP stone chakki with its motor, at today's prices.
why.plan.fees.title: Grinding fees a season
why.plan.fees: The area's grain, about {area} a day for {days} days, ground at {fee}.
why.plan.sales.title: Atta and bran a season
why.plan.sales: Your {own} a day turned into atta and bran, sold to the trader at today's prices.
why.plan.wheat.title: Your wheat a season
why.plan.wheat: The mill buys your {own} a day at today's trader price: your farm sells it, the mill pays.
why.plan.power.title: Power a season
why.plan.repairs.title: Repairs a season
why.plan.repairs: About {share} of the machine's cost each season keeps the stones dressed and the belts whole.
why.plan.depreciation.title: Wear and tear a season
why.plan.depreciation: The shed lasts about 20 years and the chakki about 10: their cost is spread over their seasons.
why.plan.wage.title: The {role}'s wage
why.plan.wage: A season's wage, paid at the start of each season.
why.plan.profit.title: Profit a season
why.plan.profit: Fees and sales less wheat, power, repairs, wear and tear and the wage.
why.plan.cash.title: Cash to put in
why.plan.cash: The building and machine ({cost}), and a season's running cash: the wage, or run by you, the power and repairs; less a business loan if you take one ({loan}).
why.plan.payback.title: Payback
why.plan.payback: The building and machine's {cost} over a season's profit of {profit}.
why.plan.loan.title: A business loan
why.plan.loan: The co-op bank lends a business up to {ltv} of its building and machine ({cost}), paid back in equal parts over {seasons} seasons from the business's own cash, with interest. You guarantee it: if the business can't pay, it counts on your credit, and closing it makes what's still owed your loan.
why.plan.interest.title: Interest on the loan
why.plan.interest: {loan} borrowed at {rate} a season: the first season's interest. It falls as the loan is paid down.
why.planHours.title: Your hours, at a day labourer's pay
why.planHours.farm: Running it yourself saves the wage, but those hours come off your farm work: fields get less care, and you can't do day labour then. The profit above doesn't count them.
why.planHours.lesson: Your own time has a price too: compare the wage you save with what your hours would earn.
why.businessOverdraft.title: Overdraft used
why.businessOverdraft.limit: Its limit: {pct} of a season's running costs
why.businessOverdraft.rate: Interest a season on what's drawn
why.businessOverdraft.draws: When its cash can't pay for wheat, power, repairs, a wage or a loan payment, the bank pays and the overdraft grows; money coming in pays it off first.
why.businessOverdraft.past: Past the limit it stops buying wheat (grinding for the area goes on), and at the close a wage it can't pay goes unpaid: the worker leaves.
why.businessOverdraft.lesson: An overdraft carries a business through a short patch, at a price; it's no way to run one.
why.businessClose.toYou: Comes to you if you close now
why.businessClose.yourLoan: Becomes your loan if you close now
why.businessClose.stock: Its atta and bran go to the trader at today's price.
why.businessClose.sale: The building and equipment sell at {pct} of what they're still worth on its books: used machines fetch less.
why.businessClose.debts: Its overdraft and business loan are repaid first; what they can't cover becomes your co-op bank loan over {seasons} seasons, because you guaranteed it.
why.businessClose.worker: Its worker leaves, and the acre is free to farm again.
why.businessClose.lesson: Closing ends a business's losses, but rarely gets back what you put in.
why.plan.lesson: A plan is a guess: after 4 seasons the mill's card compares it with what really happened.
why.handHome.title: Lives in
why.handHome.remit: Of the wage, sent home to the family in {village}
why.handHome.house: The family house, part of the pay, worth a season
place.houseHint: Tap a lit acre: an empty field you own, or the labour quarters.
why.householdHome.title: Their home
why.householdHome.lesson: A crowded home makes a family less happy: another house helps.

books.goods.bakery: Cost of the pav and rusk sold
books.why.noOwn.bakery: It baked nothing: no atta, no cash to buy it, or a mix of 0

why.businessPeople.area: The village and the hamlets around it
why.businessPeople.shops: The village grocer and tea stall sell to all of them, so your townspeople buy through the shops too.
why.recipeShops.title: The shops would buy {good}
why.recipeShops.each: A person buys in a real day (about three weeks of life)
why.recipeShops.price: They pay the trader's price that morning
why.recipeShops.round: They collect at 6:00 each morning, with the trader's truck: what was made since the last round, up to this much.

why.recipeMix.keeps: It keeps, so the trader takes what the shops don't, up to his amount.

why.businessCash.own.bakery: The bakery's own money, apart from yours: what you put in and its sales in; atta, firewood, supplies and wages out.

why.businessMarket.price.bakery: Atta your mill can't give is bought at the market's import price, with its transport.

why.plan.cost.bakery: A bakery shed with a wood-fired oven and a dough mixer, at today's prices.
why.plan.sales.bakery: What the village shops buy each morning, and the trader's rusk, for {days} days at today's prices. Bread they don't buy isn't counted.
why.plan.wheat.bakery: About {own} baked a day: its atta at what it costs today (your mill's at the trader's price, else the market's), and {supplies} of sugar, oil and yeast a {batch} batch.
why.plan.power.bakery: Each {batch} batch takes about {fuel} of firewood; rusk is baked again, so it takes more.
why.plan.repairs.bakery: About {share} of the oven and mixer's cost each season keeps the oven's bricks sound and the mixer turning.
why.plan.depreciation.bakery: The shed lasts about 20 years and the oven and mixer about 10: their cost is spread over their seasons.
why.plan.profit.bakery: Sales less atta, supplies, firewood, repairs, wear and tear and the wage.

why.books.sales.bakery: What the village shops and the trader paid for the pav and rusk.
why.books.goods.bakery: What the atta and supplies in the bread sold cost, and bread thrown away unsold. Your mill's atta comes in at the trader's price.
why.books.margin.bakery: Sales less the cost of what was sold. It has to pay the running costs.
why.books.cashIn.bakery: Sales and any cash you put in.
why.books.cashOut.bakery: Atta, supplies, firewood, wages, repairs and any cash you took out.
why.books.stock.bakery: Atta, pav and rusk in stock, at what they cost.

why.businessOverdraft.past.bakery: Past the limit it can't buy atta, so the oven stops; at the close a wage it can't pay goes unpaid: the worker leaves.
why.businessClose.stock.bakery: Its atta, pav and rusk go to the trader at today's price.

why.dairyMilk.herd: What your milking animals give in a real day, less what your house drinks.

why.dairyNeighbours.title: Neighbours' milk
why.dairyNeighbours.coop: The co-op's price for buffalo milk
why.dairyNeighbours.premium: What your dairy pays above it
why.dairyNeighbours.why: Neighbours sell to your dairy at 6:00 only if it pays a little more than the co-op; it fills the milk a day after your own.

why.dairyMilkADay.title: Milk a day
why.dairyMilkADay.herd: Your herd gives, less the house's
why.dairyMilkADay.neighbours: It keeps your milk first at 6:00, then buys neighbours' milk up to this much.
why.dairyMilkADay.yoursOnly: It keeps only your milk, up to this much: you've stopped buying neighbours'.
why.dairyMilkADay.spoils: Milk not made up by the next milking spoils, so keep only what the mix needs.
why.recipeMade.rate.dairy: The dairy handles at most this much milk a real hour
why.recipeMade.recipe.paneer.dairy: 5 litres of buffalo milk make a kilo of paneer (cow milk, about a third more): {batch} a batch, split with lemon and pressed.
why.recipeMade.recipe.curd.dairy: A litre of milk sets into a kilo of curd overnight: {batch} a batch.
why.recipeMade.recipe.ghee.dairy: 15 litres of buffalo milk (22 of cow's) give a kilo of ghee: the cream churned to butter and boiled down.
why.recipeShops.lesson.dairy: Paneer and curd sell only fresh: make what the shops take, and ghee, which keeps, for the trader.
why.businessCash.own.dairy: The dairy's own money, apart from yours: what you put in and its sales in; milk, fuel and wages out.
why.businessHours.area.dairy: The dairyman works the morning's milk in these hours; the shops collect at 6:00 what was made since the last round.
why.businessHours.you.dairy: You're at the dairy these hours, so they come off your farm work.
why.businessMarket.price.dairy: After your own milk, the dairy buys neighbours' milk at 6:00 up to its milk a day, at the co-op's price and a little more.
why.businessMarket.lesson.dairy: Stop buying and it works only your herd's milk: less made, but only your own margin.

why.plan.sales.title.dairy: Paneer, curd and ghee a season
why.plan.sales.dairy: What the village shops buy each morning, and the trader's ghee, for {days} days at today's prices, as far as the milk goes.
why.plan.wheat.dairy: About {own} made a day from the milk it keeps: your herd's at the co-op's price, then neighbours' at a little more.
why.plan.power.dairy: Gas for the kadhai, and lemon and culture: about {fuel} a batch.
why.plan.repairs.dairy: About {share} of the equipment's cost each season keeps the separator and freezer running.
why.plan.depreciation.dairy: The room lasts about 20 years and the equipment about 10: their cost is spread over their seasons.
why.plan.profit.dairy: Sales less milk, fuel, repairs, wear and tear and the wage.
why.plan.cash.dairy: The room and equipment ({cost}), and a season's running cash: the wage, or run by you, the fuel and repairs; less a business loan if you take one ({loan}).
why.plan.lesson.dairy: A plan is a guess: after 4 seasons the dairy's card compares it with what really happened.
why.books.sales.dairy: What the village shops and the trader paid for the paneer, curd and ghee.
why.books.goods.dairy: What the milk in what was sold cost, and milk, paneer and curd thrown away unsold. Your own milk comes in at the co-op's price.
why.books.margin.dairy: Sales less the cost of what was sold. It has to pay the running costs.
why.books.cashIn.dairy: Sales and any cash you put in.
why.books.cashOut.dairy: Milk, fuel, wages, repairs and any cash you took out.
why.books.stock.dairy: Milk, paneer, curd and ghee in stock, at what they cost.
why.businessOverdraft.draws.dairy: When its cash can't pay for milk, fuel, repairs, a wage or a loan payment, the bank pays and the overdraft grows; money coming in pays it off first.
why.businessOverdraft.past.dairy: Past the limit it can't pay for milk, so the co-op takes it all; at the close a wage it can't pay goes unpaid: the worker leaves.
why.businessClose.stock.dairy: Its ghee goes to the trader at today's price; fresh stock is sold off with it.

board.handWhere: Works your fields and takes your orders; lives in a hut or their own home
board.letGoOnCard: Let go from the business's card
board.youRunIt: You run it yourself. Hire someone and your hours go back to the farm.

board.postAboveWhy: Better, surer people; they ask 10% more
board.handNeedsHome: Someone from outside needs an empty hut. Your townspeople don't.

board.counteredManager: Asks for more than before: the offer shows his wage for the business
board.referenceWhy: Their last employer tells you their skill, and how they left
board.fromTown: From your town: you know them well
board.regular: Worked your fields as a labourer
board.commutes: Would come daily from a neighbouring village

board.noteHigh: Surer, and they start out glad of it

board.houseInOthersPay: The house is already part of {name}'s pay: all of this is cash

why.jobUsual.title: A {role}'s usual wage

why.jobUsual.farming: The job uses their farming skill.
why.jobUsual.crafting: The job uses their crafting skill: a careful hand at a machine or an oven.
why.jobUsual.skill: Each person asks more or less by their skill: from a fifth less for a beginner to a fifth more for an expert.
why.jobWage.title: What {name} asks
why.jobWage.usual: The usual wage for the job
why.jobWage.skill: They ask more the more skilled they are: a fifth less at skill 0, a fifth more at skill 100.
why.jobWage.above: You sent word above the usual wage, so they ask 10% more.
why.jobWage.town: They live in your town: they take what they ask or more, and often a little less.
why.jobWage.migrant: They don't know you yet: most take what they ask, fewer take less.
why.jobWage.low: Offer 10% less and they may refuse. If they do, they'll ask once for their wage instead. Hired low, they remember it until a new season pays what they ask.
why.jobWage.high: Offer 10% more and they're surer to say yes, and start out glad of it.
why.jobWage.lesson: Paying below the market saves money now and often costs more later.
why.jobReference.title: Asking their last employer
why.jobReference.what: For a small fee, their last employer tells you their skill more closely, within a few points. It takes half a day.
why.jobReference.terms: "Was let go" usually means a lazy or careless worker.
why.jobReference.lesson: Hiring is a guess. A reference makes it a better one.

why.kilnWant.title: Bricks the builds wait for
why.kilnWant.text: Every build that has started and still lacks bricks, yours, the town's and the builders': what each lacks, added up. A kiln pays when this is high.
why.kilnTrader.title: Bricks the trader sells
why.kilnTrader.text: His daily limit for the whole town ({limit} bricks) at the brick's base price moved by today's prices. What your kiln sells him is added to it.
why.kilnTakes.title: What the trader takes from you
why.kilnTakes.text: Each morning at 6:00 he buys up to {max} bricks in all from your kilns, shared between them, at his own price less a tenth, {price}. A second kiln does not sell him more. What he buys is added to his stock for the whole town's builds.
why.kilnFuel.title: Kiln fuel
why.kilnFuel.text: Wood and coal at the regional price. A brick takes {kg} kg to fire; the clay is dug from the acre and costs nothing.
why.kilnFires.title: It fires outside the Monsoon
why.kilnFires.text: Wet clay can't be fired, so the kiln stops for the Monsoon. Its wage, wear and repairs still come.
why.kilnMade.title: Bricks made today
why.kilnMade.text: The kiln hand fires {rate} bricks an hour while it is open ({hours} hours a day), as far as the yard has room; his skill moves the rate as it moves every worker's output.
why.kilnYard.title: Bricks in the yard
why.kilnYard.text: Bricks fired and not yet sold. The yard holds {max}; weather spoils none. A full yard stops the firing.
why.kilnBuilds.title: Bricks sent to your builds
why.kilnBuilds.text: Your own builds take bricks from the yard first, at what they cost the kiln to fire: no profit for the kiln, and cheaper than the trader's.
why.kilnSold.title: Bricks sold to the trader
why.kilnSold.text: At 6:00 the trader took up to {max} in all from your kilns at his price less a tenth, {price}.
why.kilnCost.title: What a brick costs you
why.kilnCost.text: The fuel in one brick: {kg} kg at {price}. Wages and wear are paid whether it fires or not, so they are not in a brick.
why.plan.sales.brick_kiln: {own} bricks a day, fired every open hour and sold to the trader at his price less a tenth, for {days} days at today's prices.
why.plan.power.brick_kiln: {kg} kg of wood and coal for every brick, at today's price.
why.plan.cost.brick_kiln: A brick clamp with a chimney, a pug mill and moulds, and a yard, at today's prices.
why.plan.repairs.brick_kiln: About {share} of the equipment's cost each season keeps the moulds, the mill and the clamp whole.
why.plan.depreciation.brick_kiln: The building lasts about 20 years and the equipment about 10: their cost is spread over their seasons.
why.plan.profit.brick_kiln: Sales less fuel, repairs, wear and tear and the wage, for a season that fires.
why.plan.cash.brick_kiln: The kiln and yard ({cost}), and a season's running cash: the wage, or run by you, the fuel and repairs; less a business loan if you take one ({loan}).
why.plan.monsoon.title: The Monsoon
why.plan.monsoon: Nothing is fired in the Monsoon, so nothing is sold. The wage, wear, repairs and interest still come.
why.plan.payback.brick_kiln: The kiln and yard's {cost} over the year's profit: three seasons that fire and a Monsoon that costs, spread over four.
why.plan.lesson.brick_kiln: A plan is a guess: after 4 seasons the kiln's card compares it with what really happened.
why.businessHours.area.brick_kiln: The kiln hand fires bricks in these hours; the trader's round at 6:00 takes what is in the yard.
why.businessHours.you.brick_kiln: You are at the kiln these hours, so they come off your farm work.
why.businessCash.own.brick_kiln: The kiln's own money, apart from yours: what you put in and the bricks' sales in; fuel, wages and repairs out.
why.businessOverdraft.draws.brick_kiln: When its cash can't pay for fuel, repairs, a wage or a loan payment, the bank pays and the overdraft grows; money coming in pays it off first.
why.businessOverdraft.past.brick_kiln: Past the limit it stops buying fuel and so stops firing, and at the close a wage it can't pay goes unpaid: the worker leaves.
why.businessClose.stock.brick_kiln: The bricks in its yard go to the trader at his price less a tenth.
why.books.sales.brick_kiln: What the trader paid for the bricks, and what your own builds paid at cost.
why.books.goods.brick_kiln: What the fuel in the bricks sold cost. Bricks still in the yard stay in stock.
why.books.power.brick_kiln: The fuel is part of each brick's cost: it shows here as the cost of the bricks sold.
why.books.margin.brick_kiln: Sales less the cost of the bricks sold. It has to pay the wage and wear.
why.books.cashIn.brick_kiln: The trader's payments and any cash you put in.
why.books.cashOut.brick_kiln: Fuel, wages, repairs and any cash you took out.
why.books.stock.brick_kiln: Bricks in the yard, at what they cost to fire.

build.cardKilnRest: Cement and timber from the trader
build.cardKilnRestAll: The rest of the bricks, cement and timber from the trader
build.kilnSaving: It would cost {saving} more with the trader's bricks.

why.build.kiln.text: This morning your kiln sold the trader these bricks at his price less a tenth. They are added to his stock for every build in town, yours, the treasury's and the builders'.

why.books.cashOut.shop: Stock, wages, rent, repairs and any cash you took out.
why.books.stock.shop: What's on the counter and in the back, at what it cost.
why.books.rent: The council's rent for the pitch, paid upfront each season.
books.why.noOwn.shop: It sold nothing: nothing put out, nobody to run it, or no cash for stock
why.businessCash.own.shop: The shop's own money, apart from yours: what you put in and its sales in; stock, rent and wages out.
why.businessHours.area.shop: Customers come between 8:00 and 20:00; open fewer hours and those hours' customers go to the other shops.
why.businessHours.you.shop: You're at the shop these hours, so they come off your farm work.
why.businessMarket.price.veg_stall: What your store can't give, the stall buys at the local market each morning, as a sabziwala does at the mandi: vegetables and fruit at the market's price. Pav, paneer and curd your bakery and dairy can't give come at the import price.
why.businessMarket.lesson.veg_stall: Bought in, a good earns only the markup: your own produce, at the trader's price, earns the most.
why.businessMarket.price.tea_stall: After your herd's milk, the tea stall buys neighbours' milk at 6:00 up to its milk a day, at the co-op's price and a little more; and its snacks at the market when your bakery has none.
why.businessMarket.lesson.tea_stall: Stop buying and it works only your herd's milk: fewer cups when you run short.
why.businessMarket.price.sweet_shop: What your dairy and mill can't give, it buys at the market's import price.
why.businessMarket.lesson.sweet_shop: Your own paneer, ghee and atta make the margin: market ones cost more.
why.businessOverdraft.draws.shop: When its cash can't pay for stock, rent, repairs, a wage or a loan payment, the bank pays and the overdraft grows; money coming in pays it off first.
why.businessOverdraft.past.shop: Past the limit it can't buy stock, so its counter empties; at the close a wage it can't pay goes unpaid: the worker leaves.
why.businessClose.stock.shop: What's left in stock is sold to the trader at today's price.
why.recipeMade.recipe.rasgulla.sweet_sho: Half a kilo of paneer, kneaded and boiled in syrup, makes a kilo of rasgulla: {batch} a batch.
why.recipeMade.recipe.atta_laddoo.sweet_: Atta roasted in ghee with sugar, rolled by hand: {batch} a batch.
why.recipeMade.rate.sweet_shop: The halwai works at most this much a real hour
shopPlace.title: Where to put your {name}

square.free: Free · {rent} a season to the council
why.shopShare.title: {name}'s share of today's customers
why.shopShare.town: Your town's people, from the middle of your houses:
why.shopShare.village: The village's people, from the square:
why.shopShare.how: Each hour, people share themselves between the shops open by their pull: a shop's share is its pull over all the shops' pulls. A shop that runs out passes the rest on.
why.shopShare.lesson: Customers weigh more than price: a shop nearby, with no queue and a good name, wins them too.
why.shopShare.rival.grocer: The village's own grocer, on the main street: the usual price, never runs out, never closes.
why.shopShare.rival.village_tea: The village's own tea stall: the usual price, open from 6:00 to 22:00; it serves 200 cups an hour at most.
why.shopShare.rival.town_halwai: The halwai in the town, 1,500 m past the square: good sweets, but a long walk.
why.shopToday.title: {name}: served today
why.shopToday.hours: People come between {open} and {close}, a little each hour.
why.shopToday.short: Some who chose it went elsewhere: it ran out or was full.
why.shopToday.all: It served everyone who chose it.
why.shopToday.lesson: A customer turned away is a sale for someone else.
why.shopLost.title: Customers no shop served today
why.shopLost.how: When every shop of the kind is closed, full or out of stock, people go without: they make tea at home or buy at the weekly market.
why.shopLost.lesson: A gap no shop fills is a chance for a shop.
why.shopPeople.title: People who shop
why.shopPeople.centres: The village comes from the square; your town from the middle of your houses.
why.shopDemand.each.veg: A person's vegetables and fruit a day
why.shopDemand.adults: Of them, those who drink chai
why.shopDemand.price: 10% dearer, and about this much less is bought
why.shopDemand.how.veg: Shared between the vegetables, potatoes most, coriander least; your pav, paneer and curd as the village shops buy them.
why.shopDemand.how.chai: A real day is about 23 days of life: a few cups a day add up.
why.shopDemand.how.sweets: Shared evenly between rasgulla and laddoo.
why.shopReference.title: The usual price
why.shopReference.veg: The local market's price for each, + {pct}: what a stall charges in the village. Your products: the trader's price + {pct}.
why.shopReference.chai: What a cup costs in the village.
why.shopReference.sweets: What a kilo costs at the town's halwai.
why.shopReference.lesson: Customers compare your price with this: cheaper wins them, dearer loses some.
why.shopPrice.title: Your price
why.shopPrice.fewer: Dearer, and some go elsewhere, and fewer buy at all.
why.shopPrice.lesson: Underpricing wins customers but loses margin.
why.shopExpected.title: Your share on a pitch
why.shopExpected.yours: Your pull: the usual price, standard, 2.5 stars, no queue
why.shopExpected.how: Your share is your pull over all the shops' pulls: the village's customers, from the square.
why.pitchRent.title: Pitch rent a season
why.pitchRent.how: Paid to the council upfront: when you open, then at each close for the season ahead.
why.pitchRent.lesson: A pitch costs rent, but the whole village passes by.
why.shopPutOut.title: {good} a day
why.shopPutOut.store: Taken from your store at 6:00, at the trader's price: your farm sells it, the stall pays. What your store can't give is bought at the local market's price, if you allow it.
why.shopPutOut.yours: From your bakery or dairy at 6:00, at the trader's price, before the village shops buy; else the market's, if you allow it.
why.shopMilk.title: Milk in stock
why.shopMilk.how: At the 6:00 milking the tea stall takes your herd's milk first, at the co-op's price, before your dairy; then neighbours', if you allow it. Yesterday's milk spoils. A stall that opens later in the day buys neighbours' milk that hour.
why.shopStars.title: {name}'s stars
why.shopStars.served: Served {pct} of those who chose it
why.shopStars.how: Each night the stars move a tenth of the way to the day's score. Serving everyone who comes is worth 2 points, standard quality 1 point and good quality 1.5 points, value up to 1 point (none at 30% above the usual price); 4.5 points make 5 stars. One day shut is forgiven; from the second in a row, a shut day scores as if nobody was served.
why.shopStars.lesson: Reputation is earned slowly and lost fast: running out, or a long queue, costs more than a cheap price earns.
why.shopQuality.title: Quality
why.shopQuality.veg: Good quality puts out only fresh produce: whatever is left at night is cleared at 6:00 as spoilage, then the day's goods go out. Standard quality keeps leftovers, spoiling at their rate.
why.shopQuality.chai: Good chai is made with full-cream milk: more milk a cup, the dearest part of a cup. The milk a day goes up with it, for the same cups. At the usual price it costs more than it brings, and a price above the usual can bring a newcomer to set up against you (an even chance each season). Good chai wins customers and stars; standard chai makes the money.
why.shopQuality.sweets: Good sweets use pure ghee and fresh paneer, and nothing is kept overnight: what's left at night is cleared at 6:00 as spoilage.
why.shopQuality.cupMilk: Milk a good cup ({standard} at standard)
why.shopQuality.lesson: Quality costs every day and pays slowly, in customers and in stars.
why.businessArea.share: The area's share that comes to you
why.businessArea.chakki: The next village's chakki's pull ({m} m away)
why.businessArea.choice: The area's farm families live round your land: they choose between your mill and the chakki by price and distance. Every coin above its fee takes a share away; grain your mill can't grind that hour goes there.
why.businessFee.share: At {fee}, the area's share that comes to you

why.report.gifts: A gift isn't a cost of your farm: your farm's profit doesn't count it, your net worth does.

school.line: A government primary school: the district pays the teacher, you pay its upkeep.
school.buildingLine: Bricklayers are raising the walls. The district sends a teacher when it's done.
school.cost: Cost, a gift to the village
school.noLoan: The bank won't lend toward it now: its room is used up.
school.loanTitle: The school, with a co-op loan
school.loanWhy: The bank lends on what you already own and earn. The school isn't yours once built, so it adds nothing to the bank's room.
why.school.title: The school's cost
why.school.building: The building: two classrooms and a verandah
why.school.gift: A gift to the village: once built it's the district's school, not yours. Your net worth falls by its cost; your farm's profit doesn't, so the bank's room isn't cut.
why.school.teacher: The district posts the teacher and pays the wage, as in any government primary school.
why.school.lesson: Public goods pay back to the town, not to the one who pays: in your people's reading, and in what they earn.
why.schoolUpkeep.title: The school's upkeep
why.schoolUpkeep.text: Paid at each season's close, a gift to the village. Short of cash, it goes unpaid that season and the district carries the school.
why.schoolPupils.title: Pupils
why.schoolPupils.children: Children of {min} to {max} who can't read yet
why.schoolPupils.text: Every child of school age who can't read goes, free. After {years} years at school a child can read.
why.schoolPupils.whole: A year at school is a whole season the school was open. A season it opened part-way through doesn't count.

why.road.status.text: A road from the village to the highway. The district builds it once the village has enough households and gives its share.
why.road.status.built: It is built: every trader price follows it.
why.road.status.not: It isn't built yet: prices follow the dirt track.
why.road.households.title: Households for the petition
why.road.households.text: The district builds a road where enough people live to use it. Every family in a house of yours, and each hand in his hut, is a household.
why.road.share.title: The community share
why.road.share.text: A road is the district's, but the village pays its share, and you pay it for the village. It is a gift: your net worth falls by it; your farm's profit doesn't.
why.road.lesson: A road pays back to the whole valley first, and to you through what you sell.
why.road.days.title: Time to build
why.road.days.text: The district's workers build it; nothing you do speeds it up.
why.road.effect.title: What the road adds
why.road.effect.track: Carting a kilo on the dirt track
why.road.effect.paved: Carting a kilo on the paved road
why.road.effect.gain: So the trader pays you more, a kilo
why.road.effect.text: Every price the trader pays you is the valley's price less what it costs to cart the goods to town. A paved road makes that cheaper, so he pays you more at your farm gate. Inputs cost the same: the dealer's price already includes delivery.
why.road.earned.title: What the road earned you
why.road.earned.text: Each time you sell to the trader, the road adds its saving a kilo to the price. This is those sums added up.
why.price.roadBuilt: The road to the highway is paved, so carting costs {paved}, not {track}.
why.price.roadNot: On a dirt track carting costs {track}. The council hall can petition for a paved road, which would make it cheaper.

why.adultClass.gift: Paid when it starts, a gift to the village: outside your farm's profit.
why.adultClass.lesson: Investing in people: a cost now, paid back in what they earn for seasons after.

why.literacy.how: Children learn at the school in {years} years; adults in an adult class.
why.literacy.noSchool: With no school, only those who came able to read can. Build the school on its plot.
why.literacy.premium: An adult who can read earns {pct} more at outside work.
why.literacy.lesson: Human capital: what people know raises what they earn, and the town with them.
