confirm.BuyChaffCutter.title: Buy a chaff cutter?
equipment.hireOutNoHand: On · no hand to drive it
equipment.hireOutLeasedNote: A lease is rented for your own fields: it can't be let on.
equipment.hireOutNote: Your hand drives it on neighbours' fields, up to {acres} acres a day at {fee} an acre, paid each morning. The diesel and wear are yours.
equipment.hireOutBroken: It broke down: it works for neighbours again when it is mended (in {time}).
equipment.hireOutWaitsRepair: It broke down and waits for its repair to be paid: it works for neighbours again once it is mended.
equipment.hirePaysNote: Hiring out helps with running costs only: the tractor itself costs {standing} a season in depreciation and upkeep.
equipment.hirePaysSum: At the most neighbours want: fees {fee}, diesel {diesel}, expected repairs {wear} a season. Depreciation and upkeep ({standing}) are more: it helps run the tractor, it never pays for it.
reject.LeasedMachine: A leased tractor can't be let on.
reject.NoHandToDrive: Needs a hired hand to drive it.
why.hireFee.title: What neighbours pay an acre
why.hireFee.day: Hiring a tractor for a day
why.hireFee.cap: Most acres they want a day
why.hireFee.how: Neighbours pay less than a day's hire because they choose when they come. A day's ploughing is about this much, and neighbours' farms are small: it does not grow with your town. The price follows the price index.
why.hireFee.lesson: Hiring out machines by the job is custom hiring: farmers who cannot afford a tractor pay by the acre.
why.hireCost.title: Diesel for neighbours' acres this season
why.hireCost.chance: Chance of breaking a day, working for neighbours ({own} on your own fields)
why.hireCost.repair: A repair ({pct} of what it cost)
why.hireCost.how: The diesel is posted each morning as Power, and a repair when it breaks. Hiring out makes the tractor break twice as often on the days it works for neighbours.
why.hirePays.title: Left over a season from hiring out
why.hirePays.fees: Fees for {acres} acres a day over {days} days
why.hirePays.depreciation: Its depreciation a season ({cost} over {life} seasons)
why.hirePays.how: It earns a little, but the tractor loses more than that a season on its own. Hiring out helps with running it; it never pays for it, so buying a tractor on a loan to hire it out loses money every season.
why.hirePays.lesson: A machine pays by saving your own labour and sowing on time. Idle days let out only cover some of the running cost.
season.MachineHire.why: Neighbours paid you for your tractor's days on their fields. The diesel and repairs it cost are in Power and Repairs.
cash.row.4040.out: Your tractor on neighbours' fields, given back
why.away.Tractor: Each morning your tractor ploughs up to the acres neighbours want, with your hand driving it. The fee is paid at once and the diesel comes off it.
irrigation.solarNote: {source}'s power is {now} a season instead of {was}.
why.irrigation.panelCost: A solar panel for the {source} costs
why.irrigation.panelSaves: It saves the {source} each season ({acres} acres)
why.irrigation.panelNever: A panel takes the power off, but a {source} this small spends so little on power that the panel would not pay for itself before the {source} wears out. Solar pays where power is dear.
why.irrigation.panelEarns: The panel pays for itself well within the {source}'s life.
why.irrigation.panelNone: No acre is on its list, so a panel would save nothing yet: it takes 80% off the power of the acres it waters.
confirm.FitSolarPanel.title: Fit a solar panel?
life.notYet: The town is read at each season's close. Come back after the next one to see how your town's name stands.
life.approval: How content people are with you
life.approvalNote: It starts at 50. In this phase it only draws families or turns them away: it changes no tax and no vote.
life.pull.same: Families come as often as they always did.
life.pull.withGrants: {families} and the district's grants are {g}% higher.
life.crimeNote: A pressure on happiness and land value, never a theft: nobody loses money to it.
life.ratio: The richest tenth of your families earn {n} times the poorest
life.ratioNote: Compared a person at a time, among families with someone of working age.
life.ratioFew: Too few families to compare yet
life.part.0.1: Homes with clean water in reach: {v}%
life.part.1.0: A low business tax (none scores 100, the top rate 0): {v}
life.part.1.1: Open businesses that made a profit last season: {v}%
life.part.1.2: The road (a track, or the paved link road): {v}
life.part.2.1: Homes within reach of the school: {v}%
life.part.3.0: Homes within reach of a staffed clinic: {v}%
life.part.3.1: Health care need met, on average: {v}%
life.part.4.0: Homes with no kiln smoke on them: {v}%
life.part.4.2: Homes within reach of a collection post: {v}%
why.life.approval.title: Approval
why.life.approval.start: Approval starts at 50 when the town becomes a Township
why.life.approval.text: Each season approval moves with happiness: a content town drifts up, a sour one down. It only draws or turns away families in this phase.
why.life.score.title: {name}
why.life.score.text.0: A visitor notices first whether people are content, have water and a roof.
why.life.score.text.1: A low tax, shops that make money and a paved road make a good place to open one.
why.life.score.text.2: Reading, a school within reach and children in class.
why.life.score.text.3: A clinic with a doctor in reach, care that is met and a department that is paid.
why.life.score.text.4: Drains and a collection post are built from the Infrastructure section; a kiln's smoke lowers it.
why.life.pull.title: What your name does
why.life.pull.grants: The district's grants are higher by
why.life.pull.text: Approval and your name draw families. At 50 and 50 nothing changes, and a town left alone is never worse off.
why.life.crime.title: Crime
why.life.crime.unemployed: {n}% of working-age adults have no town job, 2 points each
why.life.crime.inequality: Inequality scores {n} of 100, three tenths of it
why.life.crime.watchman: The watchman, in his reach, takes off
why.life.crime.text: Jobs and fair wages lower crime everywhere and cost less for each point than a watchman, who only watches the streets near his post.
why.life.ratio.title: Inequality
why.life.ratio.rich: The richest tenth earn, a person, a season
why.life.ratio.poor: The poorest tenth earn, a person, a season
why.life.ratio.felt: A family below the middle loses
why.life.ratio.few: It is read from {n} families of your own.
why.life.ratio.text: Up to {n} times nobody feels it. Each whole point above costs a family below the middle a point of happiness, and from {max} the poorest start to look elsewhere.
why.life.acre.title: Crime on this acre
why.life.acre.text: Safer acres are worth more and unsafe ones less, by up to a tenth.
overlay.crime.noteLive: Crime as the town was read at the last close. The watchman's reach is lower. Tap an acre for its number.
overlay.crime.lineWatched: The town's crime is {town}; the watchman takes off {less} here.
why.landValue.crime: Crime here: safer streets are worth more, unsafe ones less
event.ReputationRead: The town was read at the close.
petition.none: No one is asking for anything you haven't given.
petition.raised: Raised at the last close by {n}.
petition.promised: Promised for the {close} close. Kept: {kept}. Broken: {broken}.
petition.topic.0.one: {n} family on the {side} side can't reach the clinic
petition.topic.0.other: {n} families on the {side} side can't reach the clinic
petition.topic.1.one: {n} family on the {side} side has a child who can't get to school
petition.topic.1.other: {n} families on the {side} side have children who can't get to school
petition.topic.2.one: {n} family on the {side} side has no community hall to go to
petition.topic.2.other: {n} families on the {side} side have no community hall to go to
petition.topic.3.one: {n} family on the {side} side feels unsafe with no watchman near
petition.topic.3.other: {n} families on the {side} side feel unsafe with no watchman near
petition.topic.4.one: {n} family on the {side} side has no playground for its children
petition.topic.4.other: {n} families on the {side} side have no playground for their children
petition.topic.5.one: {n} family on the {side} side has no clean water near
petition.topic.5.other: {n} families on the {side} side have no clean water near
petition.topic.6.one: {n} family pays over a quarter of its income in rent
petition.topic.6.other: {n} families pay over a quarter of their income in rent
petition.topic.7.one: {n} family has no work in town
petition.topic.7.other: {n} families have no work in town
petition.promiseNote: Keep it and approval rises {kept}. Break it and it falls {broken}: a broken promise is worse than silence. Doing the thing answers it with no promise at all.
confirm.AnswerPetition.title: Decline this petition?
confirm.AnswerPetition.again: The families raise it again after
reject.PetitionClosed: That petition has been answered already.
why.life.approval.step: Happiness moves it a little each close (at most {max})
why.life.approval.endings: Petitions ending: done, kept, declined, ignored or broken
why.life.petition.title: Why this petition
why.life.petition.count: Families who share the need now
why.life.petition.needed: Families it takes to raise a petition (three, or a fifth of your families)
why.life.petition.answer: Answered by promising a date or declining
why.life.petition.text.0: Building the clinic nearer, or in reach, answers it by itself.
why.life.petition.text.1: A school open and within reach of the children answers it by itself.
why.life.petition.text.2: A community hall with its caretaker, in reach, answers it by itself.
why.life.petition.text.3: A watchman's post with its watchman, in reach, answers it by itself.
why.life.petition.text.4: A playground in reach of the children answers it by itself.
why.life.petition.text.5: A well, the tower or the pond in reach answers it by itself.
why.life.petition.text.6: Rent that eases, or families who earn more, answers it by itself.
why.life.petition.text.7: Work for these families, at your business or a hand's job, answers it by itself.
festival.needsKeeper: The hall needs its caretaker in post.
festival.fromMidnight: The day starts at 0:00 and lasts the whole day.
festival.costNote: {per} coins for each of your {people} people
festival.does: For the day nobody works: everyone rests at the venue, and only the stalls stay open. Happiness +{in} within {m} m of the venue and +{out} elsewhere. Chai and sweets sell {chai} more, vegetables {veg}.
confirm.ScheduleFestival.title: Hold this festival?
confirm.ScheduleFestival.guardOk: The town still pays its bills
confirm.ScheduleFestival.giftNote: A gift to the village: outside your farm profit.
confirm.ScheduleFestival.warn: It can't be undone once it is scheduled.
reject.FestivalThisSeason: This season's festival is already planned.
reject.VenueNotReady: The community hall needs its caretaker first.
why.festival.title: What a festival costs
why.festival.people: People it is for: your families and the old village
why.festival.lift: One day: happiness within the venue's reach, then elsewhere
why.festival.shops: Chai and sweets sell more that day, vegetables a little
why.festival.text: It is paid at once, outside the town, so a festival is a real choice. On the day nobody works: hands, labourers and your own day labour rest, nobody earns outside wages, and only the stalls stay open. It can't be undone once it is scheduled.
reject.EventClosed: That card has gone: it was answered, or its time ran out.
reject.ChoiceNotAvailable: That choice can't be taken now.
event.EventRaised: Something has happened in the town.
event.ChronicleWritten: A line was added to the Chronicle.
event.drought.title: Drought
event.drought.about: No rain for {dry} days and the soil is drying fast. Your {acres} of rain-fed land will suffer.
event.drought.why.0: Dry spells in Spring and Summer can turn into a drought.
event.drought.why.1: It came because it has not rained for days, and a longer dry spell makes it more likely.
event.drought.why.2: It came because it has not rained for a long time.
event.drought.hint.ride: No cost · rain-fed standing crops lose about {pct}% of their yield
event.drought.hint.tankers: {unit} an acre for {acres} of rain-fed land · no loss
event.heatwave.title: Heatwave
event.heatwave.about: A heatwave is on. The standing crops are wilting in the heat.
event.heatwave.why.0: Heatwaves come in the hot weather.
event.heatwave.why.1: It came because it is Summer, when heatwaves are most likely.
event.heatwave.hint.ride: No cost · standing crops lose about {pct}% of their yield
event.hailstorm.title: Hailstorm
event.hailstorm.about: Hail has beaten the fields: {hit} of your standing fields are damaged.
event.hailstorm.why.0: A storm in the Monsoon can bring hail, with no warning.
event.hailstorm.hint.keep: No cost · the damaged fields keep what is left of their crop
event.hailstorm.hint.resow: New seed for the damaged fields · they start again and are ready later
event.waterlogging.title: Waterlogging
event.waterlogging.about: Many hours of heavy rain have left the low fields under water.
event.waterlogging.why.0: Long heavy rain in the Monsoon waterlogs the wettest fields.
event.waterlogging.hint.drain: No cost · the fields standing wet lose about {pct}% of their yield
event.waterlogging.hint.dig: Drains carry the water off · no loss
event.price_boom.title: Price boom
event.price_boom.about: The trader will pay {pct}% more for {crop} for {days} days.
event.price_boom.why.0: Prices swing from time to time.
event.price_boom.why.1: It came because the price is below its usual level for the season.
event.price_boom.hint.hold: No cost · what you sell in these days sells for more
event.price_boom.hint.sell: Sell what you hold to the trader today, at the higher price
event.price_slump.title: Price slump
event.price_slump.about: The trader will pay {pct}% less for {crop} for {days} days.
event.price_slump.why.0: Prices swing from time to time.
event.price_slump.why.1: It came because the price is above its usual level for the season.
event.price_slump.hint.hold: No cost · wait for the price to come back
event.price_slump.hint.sell: Sell what you hold to the trader today, at the lower price
event.fuel_spike.title: Fuel spike
event.fuel_spike.about: Diesel and power cost {pct}% more for the rest of the season.
event.fuel_spike.why.0: Fuel prices jump now and then.
event.fuel_spike.why.1: It came because prices rose by 5% or more last season.
event.fuel_spike.hint.pay: No cost now · your diesel and power bills are {pct}% dearer this season
event.fuel_spike.hint.park: Your tractor stays in the shed this season, so it burns none of the dearer diesel
event.supplier_strike.title: Supplier strike
event.supplier_strike.about: The suppliers of your {business} are on strike: its inputs cost {pct}% more for {days} days.
event.supplier_strike.why.1: It came because the town is unhappy.
event.supplier_strike.hint.pay: No cost now · its inputs are {pct}% dearer for {days} days
event.supplier_strike.hint.pause: It makes nothing for {hours} hours · no extra cost
event.supplier_strike.hint.second: No extra cost now · a strike next season costs half as much
event.health_inspection.title: Health inspection
event.health_inspection.about: An inspector is checking the kitchen of your {business}.
event.health_inspection.why.0: Food businesses are inspected from time to time.
event.health_inspection.why.1: It came because its stars are low.
event.health_inspection.hint.fine: A small fine · an inspector may come again
event.health_inspection.hint.fix: It costs more now · no inspection for a year
event.viral_rush.title: Viral rush
event.viral_rush.about: Word has spread about your {business}: more customers come in for a day.
event.viral_rush.why.0: Busy shops with good stars get talked about.
event.viral_rush.why.1: It came because your shop has good stars, and well-liked shops get talked about.
event.viral_rush.hint.carry: No cost · the stock you have serves about half of the extra customers
event.viral_rush.hint.stock: Extra ingredients so everyone who comes is served
event.breakdown.title: Breakdown
event.breakdown.why.0: Machines and equipment break down now and then.
event.breakdown.why.1: It came because its maintenance was skipped.
event.breakdown.hint.wait: No cost · it works again in {hours} hours
event.skilled_migrant.title: Skilled migrant
event.skilled_migrant.about: A skilled worker from another village has heard of your farm and wants a job. He asks for more than the going wage.
event.skilled_migrant.why.0: A good name as an employer draws skilled people.
event.skilled_migrant.why.1: It came because you have a good name as an employer.
event.skilled_migrant.hint.hire: He joins the applicants for your open post at once, with no post fee
event.wedding.title: Wedding
event.wedding.why.0: The more families you have, the more weddings there are.
event.wedding.why.1: It came because you have many families, and more families mean more weddings.
event.wedding.hint.gift: That family is happier (+{points}) and the town thinks better of you
event.dispute.title: Dispute
event.dispute.about: {a} and {b} are quarrelling over a boundary.
event.dispute.why.1: It came because the town has high inequality or low happiness.
event.dispute.why.2: It came because the town is unhappy.
event.dispute.hint.pass: No cost · both families are unhappy for a season (−{points})
event.dispute.hint.mediate: You give an hour of your day · both families are happier (+{points})
event.dispute.hint.side: One family is pleased (+{points}), the other is angry (−{points})
event.new_family.title: A family at the door
event.new_family.about: A family is looking for a home, and one of your houses stands empty.
event.new_family.why.0: The more livable your town, the more families come.
event.new_family.why.1: It came because your town is livable, and a livable town draws families.
event.new_family.hint.welcome: They move into the empty house and pay rent from the next close
event.regional_grant.title: Regional grant
event.regional_grant.about: The district gives grants to farms with a sound record. Apply, and if your books and credit are sound at the next close you receive {grant}.
event.regional_grant.why.0: A profitable last season and a good business climate bring grants.
event.regional_grant.why.1: It came because your town has a good business climate.
event.regional_grant.hint.apply: The paperwork costs a little now · {grant} at the next close if your books and credit are sound, nothing if they are not
event.land_auction.title: Land auction
event.land_auction.about: A neighbour's {size} beside your land is up for auction.
event.land_auction.why.0: Land beside yours comes up for sale from time to time.
event.land_auction.hint.bid: Buy it for {price}, 85% of its land value
event.fire.title: Fire risk
event.fire.about: Dry straw and the heat: a fire may start in one of your {n} buildings.
event.fire.why.0: Fires are rare, but when one starts it can take a building.
event.fire.why.1: It came because it is Summer and a heatwave is on or has just passed.
event.fire.hint.nothing: No cost · a fire takes about a third of a building's worth, half that inside the tower's reach
event.fire.choice.prepare: Clear dry straw, keep buckets ready
event.fire.hint.prepare: Halves the damage of any fire
event.epidemic.title: Epidemic
event.epidemic.about: A sickness is spreading in the district. For {epiDays} days families will fall ill more often.
event.epidemic.why.0: Sickness spreads where there is no clean water or no clinic.
event.epidemic.why.1: It came because some of your families have no water within reach.
event.epidemic.why.2: It came because no staffed clinic reaches your families.
event.epidemic.hint.run: No cost · a staffed clinic halves the extra sick days where it reaches
event.epidemic.hint.camp: {unit} a person for {people} people · fewer fall ill
event.epidemic.choice.close: Close the school and the shops
event.epidemic.hint.close: No cost · fewer fall ill, but the shops sell much less for {closeDays} days
event.fire_repair.title: Fire damage
event.fire_repair.about: A fire has damaged the {building}. The repair bill is {bill}.
event.fire_repair.why.0: How the damage was worked out is in the ? next to this.
event.fire_repair.hint.now: The whole bill · back at work in {fireDays} days
event.fire_repair.hint.slow: Half the bill · back at work in {slowDays} days
event.timer: If you do not answer: {choice} in {time}
event.timerStrike: It strikes in {time}, at 6:00, and only while you are here. It never strikes while you are away.
events.title: Events
menu.events.note: What waits for an answer, and your last answers
away.eventDefault: You were away, so the safe choice was taken: {choice}. {effect}
away.grantRefused: The regional grant did not come: your books or credit were not sound.
away.eventsNote: No big event or disaster can start while you are away.
confirm.AnswerEvent.title: Pay for it?
why.event.title: Why did this come?
why.event.oddsMinor: Something small comes on about 9 days in 10.
why.event.oddsMajor: A big event comes about once a game year.
why.event.oddsDisaster: Disasters are rare: about one big event in 16 days is a fire or an epidemic.
why.event.text: Every choice is yours. If you do not answer, the first choice, which costs nothing, is taken when the time runs out. Preparing costs coins now and saves more later.
why.event.textDisaster: A disaster is warned two days ahead so you can prepare. It strikes only while you are here, never while you are away.
why.fire.title: The fire's damage
why.fire.text: A building that is a home, a shed or a stall's stand keeps working while it is repaired; a business building is shut while it burns.
why.eventHist.title: What it cost
why.eventHist.howDefault: for you: its time ran out, or you were away, so the first choice was taken
why.eventHist.text: An answer is final. Choices that cost nothing are always there, so you can never be forced into a spend.
event.drought.prep: Your pump or well keeps {n} of your standing fields watered. They are not affected.
event.fire.prep: The water tower reaches {tower} of your {n} buildings.
event.fire.prepNone: No water tower reaches your {n} buildings yet.
event.epidemic.prep: A staffed clinic covers {n} of your {all} families and halves the extra sick days there.
event.epidemic.prepNone: No staffed clinic reaches your families yet.
insurance.title: Insurance
insurance.cropOn: About {pct} of a crop's value, charged when you sow. Pays when luck takes more than {excess} of the yield.
insurance.cropOff: Off. Crops you sow now are not insured.
insurance.noBuildings: No buildings of yours to insure yet
insurance.propertyOn: On since the last close. Pays {pct} of a fire's repair bill.
insurance.propertyOff: Off. A fire would cost you the whole repair bill.
insurance.businessOn: Pays {pct} of a fire's repair bill and {days} of each day shut.
insurance.businessOff: Off. A fire or a paused line would cost the business its repair bill and its lost days.
insurance.offPaid: Off now. No refund for the season already paid.
insurance.bizPremium: {premium} a season, from its own cash
sow.insured: Insured: premium {premium}, pays if luck takes more than {excess} of the yield.
sow.notInsured: Not insured: you do not have the cash for the premium.
season.due.insurance.why: The premium for your buildings' insurance for the season that begins, taken at the close. If your cash can't pay it, the policy ends: it is never a debt.
season.InsuranceClaims.why: What crop insurance paid when luck (weather, pests or an event) took more than the excess from a harvest.
season.CropInsurancePremiums.why: The premiums charged when you sowed an insured crop: a small part of what its harvest is worth.
season.InsuranceClaimsReceived.why: What property and business insurance paid after a fire or a paused line. Outside farm profit.
season.InsurancePremiums.why: The premiums for your buildings' insurance, charged at the close. Outside farm profit.
season.RegionalGrants.why: A grant the region paid after you applied. Outside farm profit.
season.DisasterLoss.why: What a fire's repair cost you. Outside farm profit.
season.EventCosts.why: What you paid to soften an event: tankers, drains, a fine, a second supplier. Outside farm profit.
away.insuranceLapsed: Your {what} ended: the cash could not pay its {premium} premium.
away.cropNotInsured: Your {crop} was sown uninsured: the cash could not pay the {premium} premium.
event.InsuranceLapsed: A policy ended: its premium could not be paid.
event.CropNotInsured: A crop was sown without insurance.
reject.NoBuildings: You have no buildings of yours to insure yet.
cash.row.4355.in: Insurance paid for a fire or a pause
why.insCrop.title: Crop insurance
why.insCrop.policy: A season policy for each crop you sow while it is on
why.insCrop.pays: Pays when weather, pests or an event take more than {excess} of the yield
why.insCrop.premium: The premium is charged when you sow, from your cash
why.insCrop.text: Insurance covers luck, not neglect: a field you did not water, tend or feed pays no claim. If your cash can't pay the premium at sowing, the crop goes uninsured.
why.insProp.title: Property insurance
why.insProp.worth: What your buildings are worth on your books
why.insProp.rate: The premium is {pct} of that a season
why.insProp.pays: A fire's repair bill: it pays
why.insProp.text: It is paid at each close for the season that begins. Switched on mid-season, it starts at the next close; switched off, it ends at once with no refund. A fire already warned of before the cover began is not paid. Unpaid, the policy ends: it is never a debt.
why.insBiz.title: Business insurance
why.insBiz.worth: The building and equipment are worth
why.insBiz.total: The business pays, from its own cash
why.insBiz.fire: A fire's repair bill: it pays
why.insBiz.day: Each day shut pays {pct} of the day's average profit
why.insBiz.text: The business pays its own premium at the close; unpaid, the policy ends. It pays for a fire and for a paused line, not for a slow season.
why.insClaim.title: Why this was paid
why.insClaim.under: You are paid when it falls under
why.insClaim.sum: {sum} insured, paid for each of the {gap} points under
why.insClaim.textCrop: Soil, water, care and seed are not insured: only weather, pests and events count.
why.insClaim.pause: A paused line: {days} days shut, {pct}% of the lost profit
why.insClaim.textFire: You carry the rest of the repair bill. A fire already warned of before the cover began is not paid.
why.insPremium.title: The crop insurance premium
why.insPremium.sum: What the harvest is worth at the trader's floor price
why.insPremium.pests: Pests: some of these crops get an outbreak that costs part of the yield
why.insPremium.events: Hail, drought and waterlogging: a flat {pct} of that value
why.insPremium.text: The premium is priced a little above what the insurer expects to pay out, so on average insurance costs you a little. It is for the one bad year.
contract.title: Fixed-price contract
contract.noOffers: No offer now. At each close the trader offers a fixed price for your two biggest harvests of wheat, rice, maize, mustard, lentils or potato, if each was {kg} kg or more.
alert.contractOffers: The trader offers you a fixed price for your {crops}.
away.contractOffered: The trader offers a fixed price for {qty} of your {crop}: {price}. See the Store.
away.contractDone: Your {crop} contract closed: {filled} of {qty} delivered, nothing to pay.
away.contractShort: Your {crop} contract closed: {filled} of {qty} delivered, and you paid {amount} for the rest.
confirm.AcceptContract.title: Fix this price?
confirm.AcceptContract.binding: This is binding. In {season} the first {qty} of {crop} you sell to the trader are paid at this price. If you sell less, and the price has risen, you pay the difference for what is missing.
season.due.contract.why: What a fixed-price contract costs because you did not deliver all of it and the price rose, plus any shortfall carried from before. Taken when the season closes, after your loans.
season.short.contract: the shortfall would be carried to the next close
season.ContractSettlement.why: What you paid because you sold the trader less than a contract's quantity and the price had risen above the contract's.
why.conOffer.title: A fixed price for {good}
why.conOffer.expected: The price the trader is expected to pay in {season}
why.conOffer.discount: You give up {pct} to know it now
why.conOffer.text: A fixed price is certainty with a small cost: it is {pct} under what the trader is expected to pay, whatever happens to the market. If the price rises you still get this one; if you sell less than the quantity and the price rose, you pay the difference for the missing kilos.
why.conOpen.title: Your {good} contract, against the market
why.conOpen.gain: What the delivered kilos paid more or less than the market
why.conOpen.short: What the missing kilos would cost now (the season's average price is {avg})
why.conOpen.textRunning: The first kilos you sell to the trader this season are paid at the fixed price, whichever you choose. At the close, each kilo still missing costs you what the season's average price rose above the fixed one. If the price fell, the missing kilos cost nothing.
why.conOpen.textWaiting: It starts when its season begins. Sell the trader this crop then and the first kilos are paid at the fixed price.
why.conDone.title: Your {good} contract, against the market
why.conDone.text: What the delivered kilos paid above or below the market, less what you paid for the kilos not delivered. Over many contracts a fixed price is no better than waiting: it only buys certainty.
why.conDue.title: Contract shortfalls at the close
why.conDue.text: Taken first when the season closes. What your cash cannot pay is carried to the next close.
reject.OfferLapsed: That offer ended at the close.
reject.TooManyContracts: You already hold the most contracts for that season.
reject.AlreadyContracted: You already have a contract for that crop in that season.
event.ContractFilled: Some of a contract was delivered.
store.contractNote: Your contract: the first {kg} are paid {price}
why.businessVillage.title: {good} at the village stall
why.businessVillage.floor: The trader's price: the village pays at least this, or the mill keeps its atta
why.businessVillage.demand: The village buys about this much a day
why.businessVillage.order: Your bakeries get their atta first, then the trader takes up to his daily amount; only what is left is offered to the village, spread over the day.
why.businessVillage.rule: The village market is small: when the mill offers more than it buys, the price falls, and the mill never sells below what the truck pays.
invoices.stopped: Your {seller} stopped delivering {good}: an invoice of {amount} is overdue.
invoices.stoppedNote: It starts again when the {name} pays. Its cash is {cash} and its overdraft is used up.
invoices.none: Nothing is owed either way. Sales to your other businesses and to the village shops are invoiced from the Township.
books.bridgeNow: Why cash moved, this season so far
books.bridgeWear: Wear and tear, not paid out
books.bridgeCustomers: Customers who have not paid yet
why.books.receivable: What your other businesses and the village shops have bought from it on terms and not yet paid. It counts in the profit now and in the cash when it is paid.
why.books.payable: What it has bought from your other businesses on terms and not yet paid. The stock is here; the money is not yet gone.
why.books.bridgeProfit: The season's profit, after tax: what it earned, which is not the same as the cash it holds.
why.books.bridgeWear: Wear and tear is a cost in the profit that no cash paid for this season, so it comes back.
why.books.bridgeCustomers: The change in what customers owe it. When more is owed than at the season's start, that part of the profit has not arrived as cash. It is shown as money not yet in hand.
why.books.bridgeSuppliers: The change in what it owes its suppliers. When it owes more than at the season's start, it has the stock and has not yet paid for it, so cash is higher for now.
why.books.bridgeStock: The change in the stock on the shelf. When it grew, flour and goods were bought and not yet sold: they took cash and are not yet a cost, so the figure is a minus. When it shrank, it is a plus.
why.books.bridgeTax: The change in tax billed and not yet paid to the town.
why.books.bridgeRunning: The profit with those differences put right: the cash that running the business itself brought in or took out. A profitable business can still run out of cash.
why.books.bridgeOther: What else moved cash: money you put in or took out, the overdraft and loans, and buildings and equipment bought.
why.invoiceTerms.title: The term for {who}
why.invoiceTerms.cash: Cash: paid at once. The buyer has the goods and you have the money.
why.invoiceTerms.term: {term}: paid {days} real days after the sale.
why.invoiceTerms.rule: You choose a term for each buyer. A longer term never earns more: it only keeps the buyer's cash longer and yours shorter. Between your own businesses it moves cash from one to the other and nothing else.
why.invoiceTerms.shops: The village grocer and tea stall are paid on the same terms and always pay.
why.invoiceOwed.title: Owed to the {name}
why.invoiceOwed.rule: A sale on terms is money you will be paid, not money you have. It counts in the profit now and in the cash on its due day.
why.invoiceLine.title: {who}: {kg} {good}
why.invoiceLine.due: Its due time, a term after the first sale of the day
why.invoiceLine.buyerCash: The buyer's cash and overdraft room now
why.invoiceLine.current: Not yet due. It is paid at its due time from the buyer's cash, then its overdraft.
why.invoiceLine.late: Past its due time and the buyer could not pay: its cash and overdraft room are short. Up to one term past due it is late; after that, overdue. There is no fee and no write-off: it stays until it is paid.
why.invoiceLine.overdue: More than one term past due. The seller has stopped delivering to this buyer until it is paid.
why.invoiceLine.shop: A village shop always pays on its due day.
why.invoiceStop.title: Why did {seller} stop?
why.invoiceStop.rule: A seller stops delivering to a buyer with an overdue invoice, until it is paid. A bakery with no atta bakes nothing, so a profitable business can run out of cash and halt.
why.invoiceStop.fix: Put cash into the business, or let its sales come in: the invoice is paid at the next hour and the mill delivers again.
ledger.boughtOnTerms: Bought from your business on terms
ledger.invoiceForgiven: An invoice forgiven when a business closed
event.InvoiceIssued: A sale on terms became an invoice.
event.SupplyStopped: A supplier stopped delivering to a business that has not paid.
alert.invoiceStopped: A supplier stopped delivering to your {name}: it has not paid an invoice.
manager.usual: About {pct} of what a worker of that trade earns a season, and a tenth of the profit
manager.boardNote: Works one business of yours himself and runs it. You choose which when you make the offer.
manager.pay: {wage} and a tenth of the profit
manager.noneYou: You run it yourself. A manager takes your place and frees your hours.
manager.noneWhy: A manager works it himself, runs it for you and reports each season.
manager.payNowNote: The base wage is paid already; a tenth of the profit comes at the close.
manager.misDaysNote: On those days only half is made or sold.
manager.letGoWhy: Then you run it yourself, or hire another.
manager.styleLine.cost_cutter: Keeps prices and costs low and holds one day of stock.
manager.styleLine.growth_chaser: Prices 5% under the reference to sell more and holds two days of stock.
manager.styleLine.quality_first: Charges 5% more for good quality and holds one day of stock.
manager.workerThere: A worker works there: let them go first, he works it himself
manager.offerSubtitle: A season's contract as manager of your {business}.
manager.offerNone: Every business of yours has a manager already.
manager.atAsked: {wage} and a tenth, what they ask
manager.missedTwice: Missed by {amount}. Missed last season too.
manager.whyMoreStock: So it never runs out, though some may spoil
manager.whyOneStock: Keeps little tied up, so it may run out
manager.why.cost_cutter: To keep costs low: a cost-cutter
manager.payThenNote: The base wage and a tenth of the profit.
manager.sour: {name} works less gladly after two misses
manager.sourWhy: A skill that grew may also bring a request for a raise.
business.managerWorks: He works it himself and runs it. Let him go from his own section.
why.managerWage.title: The manager's pay
why.managerWage.base: The base wage for a season, paid upfront from the business's cash: a share of what a worker of its trade earns
why.managerWage.skill: It follows his skill, as any worker's wage does
why.managerWage.share: Share of the profit at the close, when it is positive
why.managerWage.sofar: His share of the profit so far this season
why.managerWage.never: The share is a tenth of what the business made before it, so he never turns a profit into a loss.
why.managerWage.foot: A manager is paid from the business's own cash. He works the business himself, so there is no other worker to pay.
why.managerStyle.title: His style
why.managerStyle.stock: Days of stock or of inputs ahead
why.managerStyle.foot: No style is best for every business. He sets these each morning at 6:00.
why.managerMiss.title: Days he mis-sets
why.managerMiss.mood: A glad manager mis-sets a little less; one sour after misses, a little more.
why.managerMiss.effect: On a mis-set day only half is made or sold: a stall is out of stock, a batch is mistimed.
why.managerMiss.foot: One star loses about a tenth of the sales, five stars about a hundredth.
why.managerTarget.title: His target
why.managerTarget.profit: A profit target is last season's profit plus {pct}.
why.managerTarget.growth: A growth target is last season's sales plus {pct}.
why.managerTarget.first: In his first season it is last season's profit less his pay, so he is judged on what he adds. A goal is never a loss.
why.managerTarget.miss: He reports at each close: met or missed, and what he changed.
why.managerTarget.foot: Two misses in a row sour his mood.
why.managerRaise.title: After two misses
why.managerRaise.miss: Two missed targets in a row sour his mood for the season.
why.managerRaise.raise: His skill grows with seasons managed, and a skill that grew can bring a request for a raise.
why.managerRaise.foot: A refused raise while he is underpaid, and he leaves at the next close.
ledger.managerShare: The manager's share of the profit
reject.HasManager: That business already has a manager, and a manager's business is not run by you.
event.ManagerHired: A manager took over a business.
event.ManagerReported: A manager reported at the close.
confirm.HireManager.title: Offer this manager the job?
confirm.DismissManager.title: Let this manager go?
exit.basisHolds: What it holds is more than it earns
exit.sellRowWhy: List it, rush a sale, or open another of the same kind
exit.title: Sell or expand
exit.holdsNote: If you shut it today and paid every bill
exit.listWhy: A buyer takes {days} and pays {lo} to {hi} of its worth: {low} to {high}. It runs until the day it closes.
exit.rushWhy: Sold in a day at {pct}: {price}. You can still cancel before it closes.
exit.runsUntil: Your {name} runs until the day it closes.
exit.branchWhy: On another acre or pitch for {cost}, with its own books and manager. It starts as this one's settings. {n} of {max} branches.
exit.soldSubtitle: {buyer} paid {price}, {pct} of its worth. The acre is yours again.
exit.receiptTax: Business tax on the season's profit with the gain of {gain}
exit.receiptNote: A gain over what it held is business income this season.
confirm.ListBusiness.title: List this business for sale?
confirm.CancelBusinessSale.title: Cancel the sale?
reject.AlreadyListed: That business is already listed for sale.
reject.NotListedForSale: That business is not listed for sale.
reject.NotOpen: It is still being built: only an open business is sold.
reject.TooManyBranches: You already have the most branches of that kind.
event.BusinessListed: A business was listed for sale.
ledger.stockToBuyer: Stock taken over by the buyer at cost
ledger.buildingsToBuyer: Building and equipment taken over by the buyer at book value
ledger.saleGain: The buyer's price over what the business held
why.businessWorth.title: What it is worth
why.businessWorth.profit: A year's profit, from {n} season(s) of books
why.businessWorth.base: The usual multiple of a year's profit
why.businessWorth.growth: The last two seasons earned 10% or more above the two before
why.businessWorth.fall: The last two seasons earned 10% or more below the two before
why.businessWorth.steady: No lasting rise or fall in profit
why.businessWorth.noTrend: Under four seasons of books: no trend to read yet
why.businessWorth.risk: A season lost money, or it is under four seasons old
why.businessWorth.manager: A manager and four profitable seasons
why.businessWorth.multiple: The multiple, kept between {min} and {max} times
why.businessWorth.earns: What it earns: the multiple of a year's profit
why.businessWorth.foot: Its worth is the larger of what it earns and what it holds, so a sale never ends below what you put in and kept.
why.businessHolds.title: What it holds
why.businessHolds.assets: Its cash, stock, what customers owe, building and equipment at book value
why.businessHolds.debts: Less its overdraft, loan, tax and what it owes suppliers
why.businessHolds.foot: The same figure net worth counts for this business.
why.businessSale.title: How a sale is priced
why.businessSale.buyer: A buyer pays, of its worth then
why.businessSale.floor: Never under what the business holds.
why.businessSale.goes: The business, its building, equipment, stock and what customers owe go to the buyer. Its people are released with severance.
why.businessSale.tax: The gain over what it held is business income this season, taxed at the business tax with the season's profit.
why.businessSale.foot: You can cancel until a buyer completes. It keeps running meanwhile.
why.businessBranch.title: Branches
why.businessBranch.what: A second business of the same kind, on another acre or pitch.
why.businessBranch.books: Its own books, manager and worth. It starts with the first one's hours, prices and mix.
why.businessBranch.limit: At most {max} branches of a kind.
why.businessBranch.foot: No franchises: every branch is yours to run or manage.
confirm.ListBusiness.warn: It runs until a buyer completes. You can take it off the market any time before.
owner.title: Who owns the {name}
owner.noInvestorNote: None. One can put money in when the business does well.
owner.noPartnerNote: None. One can join; they would hold {pct}.
owner.backNote: Buying a share back costs what the business is worth now times the share, and never less than what they put in.
reject.BuyBackTooEarly: An investor's share can be bought back only after four seasons.
reject.HasStake: That business already has one of those.
reject.OutsideCap: Outside owners together cannot hold more than that.
deal.investor.title: An investor
deal.partner.title: A partner
deal.buyout.title: An offer for your {name}
deal.investor.about: {name}, a trader from the district, offers {cash} to your {biz} for {pct} of its equity and profit.
deal.partner.about: {name}, from your town, offers to put in {cash} from savings and join your {biz} as a partner with {pct} of its profit.
deal.buyout.about: {buyer} offers {price} for your {name}: {pct} of what it is worth.
deal.buyout.note: The business is sold today and its people are released. Tax is on the gain.
deal.buyout.wait: Costs nothing · the business stays yours
deal.partner.cash: Their stake, from their own savings, into the {biz}
deal.profitRow: Share of profit at each close
deal.investor.backValue: After {n} seasons, at its worth then
deal.partner.backValue: Any time, at its worth times {pct}
deal.wait: No cost · the offer goes away and may come again
deal.investor.yesNote: You can buy the share back later
deal.partner.yesNote: Their share shows in your books
deal.timer: If you do not answer: no, thank you in {time}
alert.deal.Investor: An investor offers money for your {name} · {time}
alert.deal.Partner: A townsperson offers to be a partner in your {name} · {time}
alert.deal.BuyOut: A buyer offers to buy your {name} · {time}
confirm.AcceptBuyOut.title: Sell it to this buyer?
confirm.BuyBackShare.title: Buy this share back?
why.investorOffer.title: An investor's offer
why.investorOffer.what: An investor puts cash into the business for a share of its equity and profit. The cash is the worth times the share.
why.investorOffer.min: A business must be worth at least
why.investorOffer.when: Offers come at a season close, to a business that made a profit that season.
why.investorOffer.cap: Outside owners together never hold more than
why.investorOffer.foot: You have {hours} hours to answer. No answer is no, and it costs nothing.
why.partnerOffer.title: A partner's offer
why.partnerOffer.what: A partner is someone from your town who puts in their own savings and takes a fixed share of the profit.
why.partnerOffer.profit: Their share of each season's profit
why.partnerOffer.noPrices: They set no prices and run nothing. They share the books and the buy-out.
why.partnerOffer.cap: Outside owners together never hold more than
why.partnerOffer.foot: A partner needs savings at least the stake, so partners suit small businesses.
why.dealBuyout.title: A buyer's offer
why.dealBuyout.range: Offers are this share of the worth
why.dealBuyout.floor: Never under what the business holds, so a sale never ends in a paper loss.
why.dealBuyout.open: Hours open (more if it is a big part of your net worth)
why.dealBuyout.gap: Seasons between offers for a business
why.dealBuyout.sale: Accepting is a sale: the outside owners are paid first, the gain is taxed with the season's profit and its people are released.
why.ownerRow.title: Who owns it
why.ownerRow.what: You own what no outside owner holds. An investor or a partner holds a share of its equity and profit.
why.ownerRow.books: An outside owner's money sits in the business's books as something it owes them, so your equity is what is left.
why.ownerRow.foot: Open the owners to buy a share back.
why.ownerPaid.title: What an outside owner is paid
why.ownerPaid.what: At each close, the share of the season's profit after tax, from the business's cash.
why.ownerPaid.after: A season that lost money pays nothing.
why.ownerPaid.loss: It is a share of what the business earned, not a cost, so it does not lower the profit.
why.ownerPaid.foot: A partner's share is paid into their household's savings.
why.outsideLimit.title: The limit on outside owners
why.outsideLimit.what: Investor and partner together never hold more than this, so you keep control.
why.outsideLimit.each: One investor and one partner for each business.
why.outsideLimit.foot: Buy a share back to make room.
why.shareBack.title: Buying a share back
why.shareBack.price: The price is what the business is worth now times the share, so it rises if the business grew. It never falls below what they put in, so a business cannot be run down to buy its owner out cheaply.
why.shareBack.wait: Seasons an investor's share must stand
why.shareBack.partner: A partner can be bought out at any time.
why.shareBack.sale: If you sell or close the business instead, outside owners are paid first from what is left.
why.shareBack.foot: The cash comes from your own.
why.dealOffer.title: An offer waiting
why.dealOffer.what: An investor, a partner or a buyer wants a part of a business, or all of it.
why.dealOffer.wait: No answer is no. It costs nothing and may come again.
why.dealOffer.foot: Offers come at a season close while you are playing, never while you are away.
cash.row.2500.in: An outside owner's money put in
cash.row.2500.out: An outside owner's share paid out
cash.row.3250.in: Profit paid back by an outside owner
ledger.outsideIn: An investor or a partner put money in
ledger.outsideSettled: An outside owner paid his share
ledger.outsideShare: Profit paid to an outside owner
event.DealOffered: An offer came for a business.
event.DealAnswered: An offer for a business was answered.
event.ShareBoughtBack: A share of a business was bought back.
benefit.meal.name: A meal each working day
benefit.health.name: Health cover
benefit.health.note: {cost} a worker a season · sick days halve and are paid · needs the clinic
benefit.festival.name: Festival bonus
benefit.festival.note: {cost} a worker, paid at each festival · motivation +0.04 that season, your name +1
benefit.leave.name: Paid leave, 4 days a season
benefit.leave.note: {cost} a worker and those days' work lost · motivation +0.03, tiredness −0.10 a season
benefit.keptRep: Two or more kept through a close raise your name as an employer by 1 · poaching {pct} a season
benefit.keptPoach: Poaching {pct} a season · two kept through a close raise your name
night.onNote: Wage {wage} a season · tiredness {tired} a day · the grid powers it
night.noGridNote: The grid is off, so the night shift cannot work.
night.short: Day shift behind on {n} of the last {of} days
night.startNote: A second worker at {wage} a season (a quarter more than the day's). Offered after {need} days behind. Needs the grid.
confirm.SetNightShift.title: Start a night shift?
confirm.SetNightShift.wage: The second worker's wage a season
reject.NoClinic: Health cover needs the clinic, with its doctor in post.
reject.NoGrid: A night shift needs the grid; a generator will not do.
reject.NoNightShift: This kind of business has no night shift.
reject.NightNotOffered: Not yet: the day shift has not been too busy for it.
reject.NightState: The night shift is already running, or there is none to stop.
event.BenefitChanged: A benefit was switched on or off.
event.NightShiftChanged: A night shift started or stopped.
why.benefit.meal.title: A meal each working day
why.benefit.meal.effect: Workers who eat at work are keener: motivation goes up by 3 points.
why.benefit.health.title: Health cover
why.benefit.health.effect: Sick days halve (2% to 1%) and the sick days are paid for you, so no card and nothing lost. It needs the clinic.
why.benefit.festival.title: Festival bonus
why.benefit.festival.effect: Paid to each worker on the day of a festival. Motivation up 4 points that season and your name as an employer up by 1.
why.benefit.leave.title: Paid leave
why.benefit.leave.effect: 4 days of a season's 90 are paid and not worked. Motivation up 3 points, and tiredness falls 10 points once a season.
why.benefit.cost: What it costs a worker a season ({n} workers)
why.benefit.output: In output: {pct}% of a {wage} worker's work
why.benefit.keep: In keeping people: it lowers the poaching chance, now {poach}% a season
why.benefit.rep: In your name: two or more benefits kept through a close raise it by 1.
why.benefit.foot: Benefits do not pay in output alone. They pay in keeping a skilled worker and in your name as an employer.
why.loyalty.title: Poaching with your benefits
why.loyalty.leave: Leaving unhappy is made less likely by the same factor.
why.loyalty.rep: {n} or more kept through a close raise your name as an employer by 1.
why.loyalty.foot: A worker poached at 15% over their worth costs you more than the benefits would have.
why.night.title: The night shift
why.night.what: A second worker works {from}:00 to {to}:00, with no overtime, on the grid.
why.night.offered: Offered when the day shift fell behind on this many days
why.night.wage: The night worker's wage above the role's
why.night.tired: Tiredness a day for the night worker
why.night.grid: It adds hours, not customers: a plan the day shift already makes gains nothing.
why.night.foot: Mill, bakery, dairy and sweet shop only. It stops with the day worker or without the grid.
research.tuitionFee: The fee a pupil pays a season
business.shortCash.tuition: Short of cash: it can't buy books and chalk. Put cash in, or close it.
tuition.pupilsNote: {yours} of yours · {village} from the old village
tuition.starsNote: Families send {pct} of the children they can pay for
tuition.feeNote: {fee} for the pupils who enrol next. Those in already keep the fee they came at.
why.tuitionKids.title: Children whose families would pay
why.tuitionKids.text: Your children aged {ages} whose family's schooling budget ({budget} of its income) covers the fee of {fee}, and the old village's the same way, counted as a head-count. Of them, families send a share set by the centre's stars: {take} at the {stars} stars a new centre starts with.
why.tuitionFeeRef.title: The fee
why.tuitionFeeRef.text: What a family pays for each child a season, at today's prices. A family's schooling budget is {budget} of its income, so a dearer fee fits fewer children into it.
why.tuitionPlaces.title: Places
why.tuitionPlaces.text: {batches} batches of {size} children each evening for {hours} hours in all. Any more wait: the batches fill in turn.
why.tuitionPupils.title: Pupils this season
why.tuitionPupils.text: Children aged {ages} enrolled when the centre opened and at each season's close. Your own children come first, then the old village's. A family pays for as many children as its schooling budget ({budget} of its income) covers, and sends {take} of them. A pupil keeps the place all season.
why.tuitionBatches.title: The batches
why.tuitionBatches.text: The centre teaches {size} children at a time. The first batch fills, then the second; each batch's pupils pay the day's fee when their class ends.
why.tuitionFees.title: Fees taken this season
why.tuitionFees.text: Each pupil pays {fee} a season, taken a little each evening their batch runs ({days} evenings in a season), so an evening with no teacher earns nothing. Books and chalk cost {books} a pupil a season, taken the same way.
why.tuitionStars.title: The centre's stars
why.tuitionStars.text: Stars move a tenth of the way a day towards a target: full batches count three parts in five, pupils who came back for another season two. They decide how many of the children a family can pay for are sent: {low} at no stars, all at five. Now {take}.
why.tuitionSeasons.title: Seasons your pupils have sat
why.tuitionSeasons.text: Each season a child of yours sits adds {gain} to their farming and to their crafting, up to {max} seasons. A child who grows up with it is a better hand when they come to the hiring board at 18. The old village's children are only counted, so they gain nothing you can see.
why.tuitionFee.title: The fee setting
why.tuitionFee.text: The fee for pupils who enrol next ({fee} a season). Pupils already in keep the fee they came at, so a price raised mid-season waits for the next enrolment; a family whose budget no longer covers it sends fewer children then.
why.plan.sales.tuition: {pupils} pupils the town would send now, at {fee} each for a season. A new centre starts with {pupils} and fills as its stars rise.
why.plan.power.tuition: {books} a pupil a season, for {pupils} pupils.
why.plan.cost.tuition: A classroom and benches, at today's prices.
why.plan.repairs.tuition: About {share} of the equipment's cost each season keeps the benches and boards whole.
why.plan.depreciation.tuition: The building lasts about 20 years and the equipment about 5: their cost is spread over their seasons.
why.plan.profit.tuition: Fees less books, repairs, wear and tear and the wage, at the pupils the town would send now.
why.plan.cash.tuition: The classroom and benches ({cost}), and a season's running cash: the wage, or run by you, the books and repairs; less a business loan if you take one ({loan}).
why.plan.payback.tuition: The classroom's {cost} over a season's profit at today's pupils: a centre fills as its stars rise, so the real figure usually comes sooner.
why.plan.lesson.tuition: A plan is a guess: after 4 seasons the centre's card compares it with what really happened.
why.businessHours.area.tuition: The tutor teaches in these hours, one batch after another.
why.businessHours.you.tuition: You teach in these hours, so they come off your farm work.
why.businessCash.own.tuition: The centre's own money, apart from yours: what you put in and the pupils' fees in; books, wages and repairs out.
why.businessOverdraft.draws.tuition: When its cash can't pay for books, repairs, a wage or a loan payment, the bank pays and the overdraft grows; money coming in pays it off first.
why.businessOverdraft.past.tuition: Past the limit it stops buying books, and at the close a wage it can't pay goes unpaid: the tutor leaves.
why.businessClose.stock.tuition: Its pupils go. Nothing is refunded: their fees were taken a day at a time.
why.books.sales.tuition: The pupils' fees, taken each evening a batch ran.
why.books.goods.tuition: Books and chalk used by the pupils taught.
why.books.power.tuition: Books and chalk show here as the cost of the classes taught.
why.books.margin.tuition: Fees less books and chalk. It has to pay the wage and wear.
why.books.cashIn.tuition: The pupils' fees and any cash you put in.
why.books.cashOut.tuition: Books, wages, repairs and any cash you took out.
why.citizenTuition.title: Tuition
why.citizenTuition.text: {name} has sat seasons at a tuition centre. Each season adds {gain} to their farming and to their crafting, up to {max} seasons. So far they have gained {total} in each. It stays with them: at 18 they come to the hiring board a better hand.
equipment.doesTempo: Carries {kg} a leg · {hours} h a leg · {legs} legs a day
equipment.tempoLeasedNote: A leased tempo cannot be let out: it goes back at the close.
equipment.tempoOn: On · idle legs go to neighbours
equipment.tempoLetOutNote: Legs you did not use by midnight carry neighbours' goods: {pay} a leg, less {cost} of diesel and wear. Your own trips always come first. Needs a hired hand to drive.
equipment.tempoPaysBack: Pays back in about {seasons} seasons, every leg yours
equipment.tempoPaysNote: A leg you use saves {saves} against the hired trolley. A season with every leg yours leaves {best} after what it costs to stand; let out alone, {letting}. Standing costs {standing} a season.
mandi.timeLegs: {hours} h of your day · away {away} h
away.tempoValue: Carried neighbours' goods on {legs} legs: {net} after diesel and wear
why.tempoLeg.title: A leg of the tempo
why.tempoLeg.text: A leg carries up to {kg} to the mandi and back in {hours} hours. It costs {diesel} of diesel and {wear} of wear. A load over one leg goes as two legs, one after the other. The tempo makes {legs} legs a day.
why.tempoRide.title: Who carries a load
why.tempoRide.text: The cheapest that can: your own tractor-trolley or cart costs nothing; then the tempo at {leg} a leg (up to {kg} in the day's legs); then the hired trolley at {trolley} a trip. A broken tempo, or one with no leg left today, hands the load to the trolley.
why.tempoLetOut.title: What neighbours pay a leg
why.tempoLetOut.text: Legs you did not use by midnight, out of {legs} a day, carry neighbours' goods. Your own trips always come first. A hired hand drives it, and a day it works for neighbours it is more likely to break. Only a tempo you bought can be let out.
why.tempoPays.title: A season at the best
why.tempoPays.text: The best season is every leg yours, each saving the hired trolley, less what the tempo costs to stand there: its wear over its life and its upkeep, or its lease. A season has few days, so the legs are few.
why.tempoPays.lesson: A tempo pays only for a farm that sends goods to the mandi most days.
event.TempoLetOut: Your tempo carried neighbours' goods on {legs} legs: {net} after its diesel and wear.
plan.wheat.restaurant: Rice, lentils, potatoes, atta, ghee and curd, and the cook's supplies
why.plan.cost.restaurant: A small restaurant with a kitchen, a gas stove, big pots and tawas, a counter and tables, at today's prices.
why.plan.sales.restaurant: Your share of the portions your town's and the old village's households set aside for eating out, for {days} days at today's prices: the dhaba takes the rest. The cook's day stops it at the kitchen's rate. A plan reckons on a pitch in the square.
why.plan.wheat.restaurant: Each dish's rice, lentils, potatoes, atta, ghee and curd: from your store at the trader's price while it lasts, the rest at the market's price; and the cook's supplies of spices, oil and the like.
why.plan.power.restaurant: The stove's gas for each dish cooked.
why.shopShare.rival.town_dhaba: The dhaba on the district road, 300 m from the square: the usual price, standard, 3 stars, and it serves 60 portions an hour at most.
why.shopQuality.meals: Good quality cooks with finer rice, fresher vegetables and more ghee: its ingredients cost more, and the diners and the stars notice. Standard quality makes the money; good wins customers.
research.shopDemand.meals: Portions they'd eat out a day
research.mealsDinersValue: {town} in your town, {village} in the old village
research.mealsKitchenValue: {n} portions an hour, {hours} hours a day
meals.sittingsNote: Between lunch and dinner the kitchen is shut.
meals.dishOff: Off the menu: its diners order the other dish
meals.lastDish: The last dish stays on the menu
why.mealsDemand.town: Your town: {n} households that eat out
why.mealsDemand.how: A household earning {min} a season or more sets aside {share} of its leisure money for eating out, and buys as many portions as that pays for over the season, spread over its {days} days. Households under {min} eat at home. Your restaurant gets its share of these: the dhaba and any newcomer take the rest.
why.mealsDiners.title: Households that eat out
why.mealsDiners.text: A household needs {min} a season or more to have money left for restaurants. Your town's households come from their own budgets; the old village counts as one household's budget for all of them.
why.mealsKitchen.title: Portions an hour
why.mealsKitchen.text: The cook and a kitchen hand, one wage, serve this many portions an hour over {hours} hours of sittings: about {day} a day at most. Past that, diners go to the dhaba.
why.mealsKitchen.cash: The kitchen cooks only what its cash can pay for: ingredients are bought as each portion is cooked.
why.mealsSittings.title: The two sittings
why.mealsSittings.text: People eat out at lunch and at dinner: the kitchen is shut from {from}:00 to {to}:00, and the cook's day is the hours it is open.
why.mealsDish.title: {name}
why.mealsDish.text: {part} of every {all} diners order this dish. A diner pays its price; the kitchen pays for each ingredient, the gas and the supplies as it cooks.
why.mealsDish.cost: What a portion costs to cook
why.mealsDish.buying: Rice, lentils, potatoes, atta, ghee and curd come from your store first at the trader's price, then from your businesses, then from the market at the retail price. The cost shown is at the market's retail price, the dearest.
board.businessWhere.restaurant: Cooks at your restaurant with a kitchen hand: one wage for the two
plan.sales.kirana: Atta, rice, lentils, ghee and the rest sold
plan.wheat.kirana: Staples: yours at the trader's price, the rest from the wholesaler
why.plan.cost.kirana: A small grocery: a shop with shelves and bins, a brass scale and a ledger, at today's prices. On a pitch it is the same shop; the pitch's rent is separate.
why.plan.sales.kirana: Your share of the staples the village and your town buy, for {days} days at today's prices (the market's price + 15%): atta 35%, rice 25%, lentils 10%, ghee 5%, rusk 5%, pav 10%, paneer 5%, curd 5%. The village grocer's staples take the rest. A plan reckons on a pitch in the square.
why.plan.wheat.kirana: Your store's goods first, then your bakery's and dairy's at the trader's price, then the wholesaler's at the trader's price. A kirana earns the markup and little else: it is a long, thin trade.
why.businessMarket.price.kirana: What your store and your businesses can't give, the kirana buys each morning from a wholesaler in the mandi town, at the trader's price.
why.businessMarket.lesson.kirana: Bought in, a good earns only the markup: your own rice and lentils, and your own atta, ghee and paneer, earn the most.
board.businessWhere.kirana: Weighs and sells at your kirana and keeps its ledger: one wage for the two
why.shopDemand.how.grocery: Shared between the staples by their shares: atta 35%, rice 25%, lentils 10%, ghee 5%, rusk 5%, pav 10%, paneer 5%, curd 5%. The village grocer's staples and your kirana share it by their score.
why.shopReference.grocery: The trader's price for each staple + {pct}: what a kirana charges in the village.
why.shopShare.rival.grocer_staples: The grocer's second shelf: the same staples, at the village's usual price, 3 stars. It cuts its price 5% when you take a third of its share.
why.shopShare.marketing: Marketing: your budget adds to the score
why.shopShare.khata: Khata: households under the line buy more from a shop that lets them pay later
event.KhataGranted: A household took goods on khata.
event.KhataWrittenOff: A khata balance was written off.
growth.reactsCut: It cuts its prices {pct} when you take a third of its share, and goes back up when you lose it. You have {share} today: it has cut its prices.
growth.reactsNot: It cuts its prices {pct} when you take a third of its share, and goes back up when you lose it. You have {share} today: not yet.
growth.budgetNote: Paid at once, and again at each close; it lasts only while it is spent
growth.marketFading: No budget: the score is fading
growth.marketGainNote: Customers it drew over the season, against what it cost
growth.marketNoGain: It drew nobody you can count: the money was wasted
growth.khataCreditNote: They buy now and pay at the close
growth.limitNote: The most one household can owe the shop at any time
growth.khataPays: The margin on the extra sales, {margin}, is more than the {lost} never paid: khata paid.
growth.khataNoPay: The margin on the extra sales, {margin}, is less than the {lost} never paid: khata did not pay.
growth.atLimit: At the limit: cut off until it pays
growth.late: A little is paid a season late
growth.more: Showing {n} of {of}. The old village's families are never on khata.
why.books.marketing: The budget you set for the shop's marketing, paid when you set it and again at each close.
why.books.badDebt: What khata customers never paid, written off at the close: 8% of what a household under 10,000 a season owes, 4% to 20,000, 1% above.
why.growthMarketing.title: Marketing
why.growthMarketing.per: Each {unit} you spend a season adds to your score
why.growthMarketing.size: The most it can add is about half a star or a 10% price cut: customers choose by one sum of price, quality, stars, distance and waiting, and marketing is one more part of it.
why.growthMarketing.fade: Stopped, it fades each close by
why.growthMarketing.lesson: It lasts only while it is spent. A shop that sells out gains nothing from more customers.
why.growthMarketValue.title: Is marketing worth it?
why.growthMarketValue.margin: What the shop kept of it
why.growthMarketValue.lesson: On a thin trade marketing rarely pays for itself in a season. It makes sense when the shop has room to sell more at a good margin.
why.growthKhata.title: Khata
why.growthKhata.regular: A regular is a household of yours that this shop attracts most: the nearest, cheapest, best-liked shop of its kind. Regulars may take goods on credit and pay at the close.
why.growthKhata.limit: The most one household may owe
why.growthKhata.score: Households under {income} a season add to your score
why.growthKhata.now: The lift to your score today, over all your town's people
why.growthKhata.village: The old village's families are never on khata: their households are not named, so a balance could not be kept.
why.growthKhata.lesson: Khata buys sales with credit: it pays only if the margin on the extra sales is more than what is never paid.
why.growthLimit.title: The limit
why.growthLimit.cut: Households at the limit or cut off
why.growthLimit.you: A household at its limit gets nothing more until the close has collected. You can also cut one off yourself, and allow it again.
why.growthLimit.risk: A bigger limit sells more to poorer households and loses more to those who never pay.
why.growthLimit.lesson: The limit is a seasonal ceiling on one household's debt.
why.growthLoss.title: What khata loses
why.growthLoss.under: A household earning under {income} a season never pays
why.growthLoss.above: Above {income} a season it never pays
why.growthLoss.late: A further share of what is owed is paid a season late
why.growthLoss.writeOff: What is never paid is written off as bad debt at the close, an expense on the shop's books.
why.growthLoss.lesson: Khata earns its place only if the extra sales are worth more than the losses.
why.growthValue.title: Is khata worth it?
why.growthValue.gain: The extra sales it brought: {pct} more kilos
why.growthValue.how: The extra sales are estimated from the credit sold: the tenth of kilos khata adds for households under the line. The margin is the shop's own at its last close.
why.growthValue.lesson: A 4% loss on credit is a quarter of a 15% margin. It pays when the shop sells to people who would not buy otherwise.
why.growthOwed.title: Owed to the shop
why.growthOwed.close: At the close each household pays what it can: a share is never paid, and {late} is paid a season late.
why.growthOwed.books: A customer's balance is money owed to you, not cash: it shows in the shop's books as owed by customers.
why.growthHousehold.title: {name}
why.growthHousehold.gone: This household no longer owes the shop.
why.growthHousehold.rate: The share it is expected never to pay
why.growthHousehold.cutByYou: You cut this household off: it buys for cash until you allow it again.
why.growthHousehold.open: At the limit or while it pays late it buys for cash; otherwise it may take more on credit.
ledger.khataSale: Sold on khata: not yet paid
confirm.SetMarketing.title: Spend on marketing?
confirm.SetMarketing.again: Paid again at each close, a season
supervisor.covers: Covers up to {span} hands · you have {n}
supervisor.needs: Needs {min} hands at the farm: you have {n}
supervisor.paysYes: Yes: about {amount} a season over his wage
supervisor.paysNo: Not in coins: about {amount} a season short of his wage
supervisor.paysNote: At your team and a 3-star supervisor. He pays for himself only on a big team; below that he buys fewer accidents, no quarrels for you to settle and fewer associations.
supervisor.postWhy: A supervisor is for 3 or more hands. Hire one more hand and the post opens.
workplace.letGoQ: Let {name} go? He keeps this season's pay, and your hands are no longer covered.
workplace.spared: What your supervisor has spared you
workplace.sparedNote: Accidents his half chance spared, quarrels he settled for you, associations that did not form.
workplace.noneHire: None: hire one from the board
workplace.supervisorNote: One covers up to 5 hands: +0.8% output a star, half the accidents, quarrels settled for you.
workplace.supervisorFarm: A supervisor is the farm's: a business has too few workers.
workplace.accidentsNote: Out for {hours} hours. More on a night shift, long days and skipped maintenance; a supervisor halves it.
workplace.conflictsNeed: A place needs 2 workers to quarrel.
workplace.conflictsNote: Likelier when the team is tired.
workplace.assocNote: Forms when pay is under the market, the team is tired, or your name is poor.
hr.Accident.title: {name} was hurt at work
hr.Accident.text: {name} is out for {hours}. {bill} Pay those hours as usual ({amount}, your name as an employer goes up), or don't ({amount} comes back, and they'll remember it).
hr.Accident.billCover: Your health cover paid the bill.
hr.Accident.billOwn: Your cash could not cover the bill, so they bore it themselves.
hr.Conflict.title: {name} and {other} are not talking
hr.Conflict.text: {name} and {other} have fallen out, and each blames the other. Talk to both ({hours} of yours; it settles 7 times in 10), move {other} apart (settled, but {other} did not ask for it), or let it be (both are down, and one may resign at the close).
hr.Association.title: The farm's workers ask for more
hr.Association.text: Your {n} workers have formed an association. {why} They ask for {raise} more on every wage. Accept (everyone's wage up {raise}, nothing more asked for 4 closes), negotiate (up {half} and a benefit; they agree about {agree} of the time, and if not it counts as a refusal), or refuse (their mood drops and their work is cut to {output} this season; a second refusal stops work for {stop}).
hr.Association.whyPay: Pay is under what your hands' skill asks.
hr.Association.whyTired: The team has been tired for closes in a row.
hr.Association.whyName: Your name as an employer is poor.
hr.Association.detail1: Up half as much, and a benefit
hr.Association.detail2: Mood and output down this season
away.hr.Accident: {name} was hurt at work. You did not answer, so the hours were paid as usual.
away.hr.Conflict: A quarrel at {place} was let be. Both workers are a little down, and one may leave at the close.
away.hr.Association: The farm's workers asked for more. You did not answer, so it was refused: their mood and their work are down this season.
away.supervisorUnpaid: Your supervisor left: his wage could not be paid at the close.
why.supervisor.title: What a supervisor does
why.supervisor.star: Output of each worker he covers, for each of his stars
why.supervisor.risk: The chance of an accident, and of an association, with him there
why.supervisor.quarrel: A quarrel at his place is settled for you: no card ever reaches you.
why.supervisor.assoc: An association is half as likely to form.
why.supervisor.foot: He asks about {wage} a season. He makes the hands you have a little better and a little safer; he adds none.
why.supervisorPays.title: Does a supervisor pay?
why.supervisorPays.accidents: Accidents spared, at what each would cost
why.supervisorPays.conflicts: A quarrel settled: a worker lost half the time
why.supervisorPays.spared: What he has spared you so far
why.supervisorPays.foot: In coins a supervisor pays only on a large team. Below that he buys peace: fewer accidents, no quarrels for you to settle, fewer associations. The sheet counts what he has spared.
why.accident.title: The chance of an accident
why.accident.base: A roll each day for each worker at work
why.accident.skipped: With a machine's maintenance skipped (your hands)
why.accident.half: With a supervisor on that worker
why.accident.severe: Of accidents, severe: out {hours} hours, a bill of {bill}
why.accident.out: An ordinary one keeps them out {hours} hours ({clinic} with the clinic) and the bill is {bill}, free with health cover.
why.accident.foot: Nobody dies. An accident is a bump; how you answer it is what your people remember.
why.conflict.title: The chance of a quarrel
why.conflict.base: Each season, a place of {n} or more workers rolls
why.conflict.tired: Raised by tiredness: the team's average, then {k} times that added on
why.conflict.supervisor: With a supervisor there it is settled for you.
why.conflict.choices: Talk to both: {hours} of yours, settled {pct} of the time. Move one apart: settled for certain, the one moved is cross. Let it be: both are down and one resigns {resign} of the time.
why.conflict.foot: A tired team quarrels more. Rest, a lighter order or a benefit lowers tiredness.
why.association.title: When workers form an association
why.association.when: A place of {n} or more workers can form one at a close if any of these holds:
why.association.pay: Pay is more than {pct} under what their skill asks
why.association.tired: The team's tiredness is above {level} points for {closes} closes in a row
why.association.name: Your name as an employer is under {score}
why.association.forms: The chance one forms at a close, if one holds
why.association.asks: It asks for {raise} more. If you accept, none comes again for {quiet} closes.
why.association.foot: A fair wage, rest and a good name keep workers from organising.
reject.TooFewWorkers: A supervisor is for 3 or more hands: hire another hand first.
event.SupervisorHired: A supervisor started on your farm.
event.HrEventDefaulted: A card nobody answered was answered for you.
confirm.DismissSupervisor.title: Let your supervisor go?
